description: See and hear your collaborators live while you write a song together, on the web or on your iPhone. Share your DAW or computer audio from a computer, and record the session to the song.

heading: Connection quality
text:
If a connection is weak, the session lowers the quality of the video coming in
so the audio stays smooth, and brings full quality back by itself once the
connection recovers. A collaborator with a weak connection shows a **Weak**
label on their video.

If the connection drops, the session shows **Reconnecting…** and carries on when
it can.

Web app:
If your own video freezes for others, lower **Camera quality** in the menu
beside the camera button.
description: See and hear your collaborators live while you write a song together, on the web or on your iPhone. Share your DAW or computer audio from a computer, and record the session to the song.

heading: Leaving and ending
text:
Web app:
Click **Leave** to leave. Closing the tab also takes you out of the session.

iPhone and iPad app:
Tap the red phone to leave, or end the call from the lock screen or Control
Center.

A session ends when the last person leaves. Nothing about the song changes, and
your collaborators can start a new one at any time.

So a session left open by mistake does not run on for hours, the app ends it
for you:

- **Alone.** If you are the only one in the session for 10 minutes, you leave
  it, with a note saying why.
- **Quiet.** After about an hour and a half with nobody talking, nothing
  shared, and no typing or tapping, the app asks **Still in the session?** and
  counts down a minute. Choose **Stay** to keep going, or leave.
- **Long.** After about four hours the same question appears, however busy
  the session is.
- **Five hours.** Each person can stay in a session for up to five hours at a
  time. You are warned in the last ten minutes, and then you leave it. A
  recording in progress is saved. You can rejoin straight away.

Talking, playing, or sharing audio counts as staying, so a session with music
playing from your DAW is not cut off while you work in another app.
description: See and hear your collaborators live while you write a song together, on the web or on your iPhone. Share your DAW or computer audio from a computer, and record the session to the song.

text:
Share a song and the editor grows a row of tabs. Each writer gets one, and
everyone can see everyone else's.

Nobody types over anybody. You write in your tab, they write in theirs, and the
version you agree on lives in a shared one, the Master, which takes one writer
at a time.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: Reading the tabs
text:
Web app:
On the web the tab row sits above the lyrics, and a green dot on a tab means
that writer is in the song right now. It dims when they have left. The
Collaborators section of the left panel says what each writer is doing. See
[Who is doing what](#who-is-doing-what).

| What you see | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Your name (You)** | Your own tab. Only you can type in it. |
| A star beside a name | That writer owns the song. |
| A filled dot | They are in the song right now. |
| An outlined dot | They are not. |
| **Master** | The agreed version. Anyone can type in it, one writer at a time. See [The Master](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/master/). |
| A lock on **Master** | Someone is editing it. In your colour, it is you. See [One writer at a time](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/master/#one-writer-at-a-time). |

Colours are assigned, not chosen. The owner is purple and everyone else takes
the next colour in the list, which is the same colour shown against their name
on the Collaborators screen.

A song opens on the tab you were on last time, on that device, so you come back
to where you left off.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: Watching a collaborator write
text:
Open a collaborator's tab while they are in the song and you see their cursor as
it moves: a line in their colour with their first name on it. When they select
text, the selection shows in their colour too. It all happens live, so you can
follow along as they write without either of you saving or refreshing.

Live cursors need version 2.22 or later of the iPhone app. From version 2.23
the cursor keeps pace with the words, rather than running ahead of them.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: Who is doing what
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
The Collaborators screen lists everyone on the song, each in their tab colour,
with a status under their name. A green dot means they are in the song now.
Tap a collaborator to see their profile.

Web app:
The **Collaborators** section of the left panel lists everyone on the song,
each in their tab colour, with a status under their name. On a computer, the
**Collaborators** icon at the top of the column of icons on the left edge opens
it on its own. A collaborator's row has an **Open tab** button that switches to
their tab.

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Writing in** a section, such as **Writing in Verse 1** | Typing in their own tab. |
| **Here · in** a section, or **Here now** | In the song, with their cursor in that section, but not typing. |
| **Recording…** | Recording a take. |
| **Uploading audio…** | Adding an audio file. |
| **Typing in chat…** | Writing a message in the [chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/). |
| **Performing** | In [Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/). |
| **Arranging** | In [Arrange mode](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/arrange-mode/). |
| **Looking at your tab**, **Looking at the Master**, or **Looking at** someone's tab | Reading a tab other than their own. |
| **Last edited** and a time | Not in the song. They were the last to change it. |
| **Owner** or **Collaborator** | Not in the song. |

Web app:
Writers who are not in the song right now look slightly faded, with no green
dot.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: What is yours and what is shared
text:
**Your tab is yours.** Collaborators can read it but cannot edit it. To get
your words into someone else's hands you send them, which is covered in
[Sending lines to a collaborator](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sending/). Selecting text on
someone else's tab, or on the Master while someone else is editing it, still
gives you the tools that only read it, such as rhymes, **To Me** and Genie.

**Section headers take your colour.** Write a Bridge in your tab and the header
is your colour rather than the app's purple, so a glance at a tab tells you
whose work it is.

**The Scratchpad stays private.** Nobody else can see it, on any song. It is
the right place for a line you are not ready to show.

On a shared song the scratchpad says **Private · only you can see this**, with
an eye icon. Each writer has their own. Songs shared before this worked this
way had one set of scratchpad notes for everyone, and those notes were copied
into each writer's private scratchpad, so nobody lost anything. On the iPhone
this needs version 2.21 or later.

**Recordings are shared.** Audio attached to the song is visible to everyone on
it.

iPhone and iPad app:
Each tab shows the takes belonging to that writer as a strip of
chips. When a writer has more takes than fit, the strip
ends in a **⋯ +3**.

Tap a chip and a small player appears without leaving the tab, with skip back,
play and pause, skip forward, and a close button. You can listen to how a
collaborator sang their verse while reading the words they wrote for it, which is
the point of putting the two side by side.

Web app:
On the web, a take linked to lyrics shows as a bar beside those lines in that
writer's tab, and clicking it plays it in the player pinned below the editor.
The Recordings section of the left panel lists every take on the song. See
[Recordings](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/recordings/).
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: What changes in the toolbar
text:
A shared song adds a way to talk to your collaborators.

- (iPhone and iPad) The **Chat** button appears on the right of the editor toolbar,
  with a red number when there is something new. See
  [Collaborator chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/).
- (iPhone and iPad) **Collaborators** moves off the toolbar and into the ⋯ menu.
- (iPhone and iPad) When you select text, the bar at the bottom gains **To Master**,
  **To Me** and **To Collaborator…**. On the Master tab, the bar's **Arrange**
  reads **Arrange Master**.
- (web) **Collaborators** and **Chat** move to the top of the left panel,
  and the selection toolbar gains **To Master**, **Send to…**, and **To Me** on
  someone else's tab. See [Sending lines](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sending/) and
  [Collaborator chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/).
- A live [session](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/) on the song. On the iPhone
  it is **Live Session** in the ⋯ menu. On the web it is the **Session**
  section of the left panel.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: Side by side (web)
text:
Web app:
On a computer you can read a collaborator's tab, or the Master, next to your own.
Choose **View**, then **Side by side**, or right-click a writer's tab and
choose **Open side by side**.

- **Your tab stays on the left**, and you can keep writing in it.
- **The right side shows another tab**, read-only. It has its own row of tabs,
  so you can switch between collaborators and the Master there. The × closes it.
- **Drag the divider** between them to give one side more room.
  Double-click it to make them even again.
- **Each side scrolls on its own**, so you can line up your verse with theirs.

The song remembers whether it was side by side, and what was on the right, the
next time you open it.

You can select text on the right just as on any collaborator's tab: look up rhymes
or synonyms, **Ask Genie**, send lines **To Me** or **To Master**, or link the
lines to a recording.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: If you are removed, or you leave
text:
You keep a personal copy of the song under a new title, so nothing you wrote is
lost. You stop seeing the shared version and anything written in it afterwards.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

text:
AI Style is where you tell Lyric Genie how you want it to write, once, instead
of saying it again in every wish.

Everything here applies to the whole app rather than one song. Open it from the
⋯ menu in [the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/), or from Settings.

Web app:
On the web, AI Style is a section at the bottom of Settings, and it saves when
you click out of a field.
description: Standing instructions for the AI, including words you never want it to use.

heading: Style Guidance
text:
A free-form note about how you want suggestions written. Tone, perspective,
the things you lean into, the things you are tired of.

The app's own example is a good shape to copy:

> keep it conversational. no complex language. no weather metaphors.

Short and blunt works better than a paragraph of theory. You have 300
characters, and the counter turns red as you reach the end.

This is read by [Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/) and by in-line
suggestions, so it shapes both the things you ask for and the things that
appear on their own.
description: Standing instructions for the AI, including words you never want it to use.

heading: Words to Avoid
text:
A list of words you do not want to see. Type a word and it becomes a tag;
tap the small cross on a tag to remove it.

Songwriters tend to fill this with their own tics, or with the words that
every AI reaches for. The app will still use one if it is genuinely the
strongest choice, so treat it as a strong preference rather than a ban.

The quickest way to find your list is to use Wish Workshop for a week and note
which word keeps turning up. That is the one to add.

The web app keeps your Style Guidance and Words to Avoid on your account, while
the iOS app keeps its own on each device. They are not shared, so set them up
once in each app you write in.
description: Standing instructions for the AI, including words you never want it to use.

heading: What it does not do
text:
AI Style is not per song. If you want to steer one song in particular, that is
what mood, theme and similar artists are for on
[the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/).

It is also not a filter applied after the fact. The guidance goes in before the
writing happens, so it shapes the suggestion rather than censoring it.
description: Standing instructions for the AI, including words you never want it to use.

text:
Sometimes you have two good versions of a line and you are not ready to choose.
Write both on the same line with a slash between them, and Lyric Genie keeps
the first as the line and the rest as alternates.
description: Keep two or more versions of a lyric line side by side with a spaced slash, and swap which one is the main line with one click.

heading: Writing an alternate
text:
Type a space, a slash and a space between the versions:

```
I left it all behind / I don't know why
```

The first version is the **main line**. Everything after a ` / ` is an
alternate. A line can hold more than one:

```
Out on the edge / Out on the wire / Out past the fire
```

The spaces matter. `24/7` and `and/or` have no spaces around the slash, so they
stay ordinary text. A section header such as `[Chorus]` never has alternates.
description: Keep two or more versions of a lyric line side by side with a spaced slash, and swap which one is the main line with one click.

heading: How alternates look
text:
The main line reads as normal. Each alternate is faded, and the slash before it
is coloured so you can see where one version ends and the next begins.

The text is stored exactly as you typed it. Nothing is hidden or moved, and you
edit an alternate like any other text.
description: Keep two or more versions of a lyric line side by side with a spaced slash, and swap which one is the main line with one click.

heading: Swapping in an alternate
text:
Web app:
Point at the line, or put your cursor on it, and a small ⇄ appears at the end of
each alternate. Click it and that alternate becomes the main line: it moves to
the front, and the old main line becomes the first alternate. **Undo** puts it back.

On a tab you can't edit, such as a collaborator's, the ⇄ is shown dimmed and does
nothing.

iPhone and iPad app:
Put your cursor on the line and a ⇄ button appears at its right edge. Tap it and
the first alternate becomes the main line, and the old main line takes its
place as the first alternate. Tap again to swap them back. Each swap is one step
of **Undo**.

The ⇄ only appears on a tab you can edit.
description: Keep two or more versions of a lyric line side by side with a spaced slash, and swap which one is the main line with one click.

heading: What reads only the main line
text:
Anything that has to treat the line as one line uses the main version and
ignores the alternates:

- [Lyric sheets](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/).
- Syllable counts, and the rhyme letters in the margin. See
  [Rhyme colors and margins](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/view-options/).
- Refine Context, and title suggestions.

iPhone and iPad app:
In the iPhone app, [Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/) and
[Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/) also use the main line.

Web app:
On the web, [Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/) shows the line as you typed it, with
its alternates.

[Genie](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/) sees every version on purpose, so you can ask it which
one works better.

Alternate lines need iOS 2.22 or later in the iPhone app. An older version
shows the line exactly as typed, slash and all, so nothing is lost.
description: Keep two or more versions of a lyric line side by side with a spaced slash, and swap which one is the main line with one click.

text:
Arrange mode turns your lyrics into a checklist. Instead of a cursor and a
keyboard you get a checkbox on every line, and a row of actions that move those
lines around.

It is for structure. Use it when the words are right but they are in the wrong
order, or when a verse needs to become two.
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

heading: Getting in and out
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Tap **Arrange** at the left of the bar along the bottom of
[the editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/). You can also select some text and choose **Arrange
Lines** from the bar, which opens Arrange mode with those lines already
ticked.

To leave, tap the **✕ Arrange** pill that sits just above the Arrange bar
(**✕ Arrange Master** on the Master tab). This is iOS 2.23; before that, the
same button sat at the bottom right.

Web app:
Click **Arrange** in the song bar. The pill turns into **Done**, and clicking
that takes you back to writing. On a phone browser, Arrange is in the bar along
the bottom of the editor.
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

heading: Selecting
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Tap any line to select it, and tap it again to let it go. The count in the
middle of the bottom bar tells you how many you have.

Web app:
Click a line or its checkbox to select it, and click again to let it go. The
actions sit in a bar along the bottom of the lyrics.

**Press and drag down the column of checkboxes** and every line you pass is
selected. It is much faster than tapping a run of lines one at a time, and it is
the fastest way to take a block that does not line up with a section.

Tapping a **section header** selects that header and every line under it. That
is the quick way to move a whole chorus, and it is the thing most people do not
discover on their own.

**Select All** takes the entire song, and becomes **Deselect All** once
everything is picked.
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

heading: Dragging a single line
text:
Web app:
Each line has a grip on its right. Drag the grip to pick that line up and drop
it somewhere else, without selecting anything or using the arrows. Unlike the
app, dragging the line's text does not move it. Dragging down the checkbox
column still selects a run of lines.

iPhone and iPad app:
Press and drag a line **anywhere except its checkbox** and you pick that line up
and drop it somewhere else. It is the direct way to move one line, without
selecting anything or using the arrows.

**A drag moves the line you dragged, and only that line.** It does not matter
how many lines are ticked. Drag one line while three are selected and the three
stay exactly where they are, still selected.

So the two gestures do different jobs: the checkbox column builds a selection
for the buttons along the bottom, and dragging the line itself is a separate,
immediate move.
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

heading: What you can do with a selection
text:
| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Move Up**, **Move Down** | Shifts the selected lines one position. Greyed out at the top and bottom, because there is nowhere further to go. |
| **Duplicate** | Copies the selection in directly below itself. The fast way to turn one chorus into two. |
| **Delete** | Removes the selected lines. It asks first. |
| **Copy To Scratchpad** | Sends a copy to [the Scratchpad](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/) and leaves the song alone. |

Move, Duplicate and Delete only appear on your own tab. On a collaborator's
tab you can still select lines, and copy or send them.

Web app:
The same four actions, plus Select All, are in the web's bar. On a shared song
you also get **Send to Me** and **Send to Master**; see below.

Duplicate then edit is usually faster than retyping. Duplicate a chorus, change
the one line that differs, and you have your second chorus.

Delete is the one action here that loses work. It asks for confirmation, but
undo is a safer habit if you are unsure.
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

heading: On a shared song
text:
A song with collaborators gains three more actions, all about moving lines between
people rather than around the page.

| Action | Where it sends the lines |
| --- | --- |
| **Send to Me** | From a collaborator's tab into your own. Only appears when you are looking at someone else's tab. |
| **Send to Collaborator** (iPhone and iPad) | From your tab to a collaborator you pick. They get the lines in the song's chat. |
| **Send to Master** | Into the agreed version of the song. |

These belong to the collaboration side of the app. See
[Sending lines to a collaborator](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sending/) and
[The Master](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/master/).

Web app:
Arrange on the web has no **Send to Collaborator**. To send lines to someone,
select them in the lyrics and click **Send to…** on the selection toolbar.

When a collaborator sends you lines and you click **Add to my lyrics** on their
card in the chat, Arrange opens on your tab with the new lines already ticked,
ready to move into place.
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

heading: Arranging the Master
text:
The Master tab has its own, shorter bar: **Select All**, **Send to Me**,
**Move Up**, **Move Down** and **Delete**. Tapping a section header selects the
whole section, so you move the Master a section at a time.

Only one person can change the Master at once. If someone else is editing it,
Arrange on the Master tells you to try again in a moment. See
[The Master](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/master/).
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

heading: Empty states
text:
Arrange mode needs something to arrange. If the tab is empty it says **No
lyrics to arrange**, and on a collaborator's empty tab it tells you they have not
written anything yet.

Blank lines show as **(empty line)** rather than an unlabelled gap, so you can
select and delete the spacing as well as the words.
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

heading: Not the same as selecting text
text:
Both involve picking lines, and they do different jobs.

- **Selecting text** points a writing tool at your words. See
  [Selecting and editing lines](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/selecting/).
- **Arrange mode** moves your words without changing a character of them.

If you want a line rewritten, select the text. If you want it somewhere else,
use Arrange mode.
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

text:
A blank is a gap you leave in a line on purpose. You know the line needs three
syllables there, maybe one that rhymes with *fire*, but not which words yet.
Write the rest of the line, leave a blank, and come back to it.

Lyric Genie counts a blank as the syllables it stands for, and can suggest
words that fill it exactly.

Blanks are in the web app from its first release and in the iPhone app since
iOS 2.21.
description: Leave a gap in a lyric line, set how many syllables it should be, and let Lyric Genie suggest words that fit it.

heading: What a blank is
text:
A blank is a run of underscores in your lyrics. **Two underscores make one
syllable**, so `____` is a two-syllable blank. The editor draws it as a single
coloured line with a dot between each syllable, rather than as underscores.

Because a blank is just text, it survives everything text does: syncing,
copying, exporting, and collaborators seeing your tab. A single underscore on
its own is an ordinary character, not a blank.
description: Leave a gap in a lyric line, set how many syllables it should be, and let Lyric Genie suggest words that fit it.

heading: Making a blank
text:
Any of these work:

- **Type underscores**, two for each syllable.
- **Insert Blank** in the bar along the bottom of the editor (iPhone and iPad), or
  **Blank** in the song bar (web). Each tap adds one syllable at the
  cursor, or one more syllable to the blank already there.
- **Make Blank** on a selection swaps the words you selected for a blank of the
  same number of syllables. It is in the row of actions on iOS, and under
  **⋯ More** on the web's selection toolbar.

Web app:
`⌥` `⌘` `B` (`Ctrl` `Alt` `B` on Windows and Linux) inserts a blank, and
`Backspace` beside a blank takes one syllable off it. See
[Keyboard shortcuts](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/).
description: Leave a gap in a lyric line, set how many syllables it should be, and let Lyric Genie suggest words that fit it.

heading: The blank bar
text:
Tap or click a blank and it is selected whole, and a small bar appears over it.

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **−** and **+** | One syllable fewer or more, from 1 to 8. The bar shows the count between them. |
| **Rhyme with…** | The word the blank's fill should rhyme with. It offers the endings of the other lines in the verse, with its best guess first, plus **Other word…** and **No rhyme**. |

A rhyme you set shows faintly inside the blank, as `~word`. It only lasts while
the song is open: it is not saved, and it goes once the blank is filled.
description: Leave a gap in a lyric line, set how many syllables it should be, and let Lyric Genie suggest words that fit it.

heading: Filling a blank
text:
Tap a blank and, after a moment, Lyric Genie suggests ways to fill it. Each
suggestion keeps your own words exactly and puts new words only in the gap, at
the right number of syllables. Take one and the blank is replaced by it.

Fills only appear when you tap a blank or change it with the blank bar. Resting
the cursor on a line with a blank shows nothing, so the suggestions never get
in the way of the words you are still writing.

Fills work like [in-line suggestions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/inline-suggestions/), so they
use quick AI calls. See [Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: Leave a gap in a lyric line, set how many syllables it should be, and let Lyric Genie suggest words that fit it.

heading: Blanks in Wish Workshop
text:
Select a line with a blank in it and open [Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/).
Instead of rewriting the line, it fills the blank, with the wish you pick
setting the character of the words. When the blank ends the line, the rhyme
switch reads **Rhyme with** and the word, and tapping the word lets you choose
another.
description: Leave a gap in a lyric line, set how many syllables it should be, and let Lyric Genie suggest words that fit it.

heading: How other tools treat blanks
text:
- **Syllable counts** count a blank as its syllables. See
  [Syllables](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/syllables/).
- **Rhyme letters** in the margin skip a line that ends in a blank, since there
  is no word there to rhyme yet. See [Rhyme colors and margins](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/view-options/).
description: Leave a gap in a lyric line, set how many syllables it should be, and let Lyric Genie suggest words that fit it.

text:
Genie is a chat that lives beside your song. Ask it about a line, tell it where
you are stuck, or ask for a way into the next verse. It reads the song as it is
right now, so you never have to paste your lyrics in.

It is built to help you write your song, not to write it for you. Expect
questions, options and short notes on what is working. Ask for a whole verse
and it will write one, but it will not volunteer it.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: Opening Genie
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Genie is in the iPhone app since iOS 2.22. Any of these opens it, as a sheet
over the song that you can drag taller or shorter:

- **Genie** in the bar along the bottom of the editor.
- **Genie** at the end of the row of actions when you have text selected. The
  selection goes with your next message.

Web app:
Any of these opens the Genie chat in the right-hand panel:

- **The Genie icon** at the top of the column of icons on the right edge of the
  window.
- **The floating genie** in the bottom corner of the lyrics.
- **Ask Genie** in the toolbar that appears over a selection. The selected
  lines go with your next message.
- **Not sure where to start?** on [Home](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/home/), which opens a new song
  with your first message already sent.

Click the Genie icon again to close the panel.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: One chat per song
text:
Each song has its own chat, and it is still there when you come back. It is
the same chat in both apps, so a conversation you start on the web carries on
on your iPhone. Your chat on a shared song is yours alone: collaborators have
their own, and do not see what you asked.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: Asking how Lyric Genie works
text:
Genie can also answer questions about the app itself, such as "how do I invite
someone?" or "where did my recording go?". It looks the answer up in these
docs and links to the page, and the link opens in a new tab.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: Reading the chat
text:
Genie's replies type out smoothly as they arrive, with Genie's icon beside them
on the left. New messages scroll into view at the bottom, as in a messaging
app. If you have scrolled up to read something earlier, the chat stays where
you are and a **Scroll** button with a down arrow takes you back down to the newest message.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: What Genie can see
text:
Every message you send carries a snapshot of the song:

- the title and the [AI Context](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/workspace/#the-left-panel-the-song),
- your lyrics,
- on a shared song, your collaborators' tabs and the Master,
- the scratchpad,
- your [AI Style](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/ai-style/) guidance and words to avoid.

It always reads the latest version, so if you rewrote a line since your last
message, Genie sees the new one.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: Asking about particular lines
text:
Select lines in your lyrics while the Genie panel is open, or use **Ask Genie**
on a selection (**Genie** in the iPhone app's selection row), and they are
attached to your next message. They show above the
message box with a paperclip, and Genie takes your message to be about them.
The × beside them takes them off again.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: Rhymes and syllable counts
text:
When Genie talks about rhymes or syllables, it does not guess. It looks rhymes
up in the same engine as the [rhyme sheet](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/rhymes/), and counts
syllables with the app's own counter, before it answers. While it does, the
panel says what it is checking, such as *Checking rhymes for "noon"*.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: Edit cards
text:
When Genie suggests a concrete change, it comes as a card rather than as text
for you to copy. A card can replace a line, add a line after another, add lines
at the end, or change the title or one of the AI Context fields. The old text
is struck through above the new.

**Nothing changes until you apply it.**

- **Apply** makes the change. It is one step, so undo takes it back.
- **Dismiss** sets the card aside.
- **Apply all** appears when a reply has more than one card.
- If the line appears more than once in your lyrics, the card offers **Apply to
  first** or **Apply to all**.

If you have changed the line since Genie suggested the edit, the card says so
rather than guessing where it should go. Undo an applied edit and the card
offers **Apply again**.

Edits only apply to your own tab. On a collaborator's tab or the Master, the cards
are there to read.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: Reply chips
text:
When there is an obvious next step, Genie offers two or three short replies
under its message. Tap or click one to send it as it is. On the web, the
pencil beside it puts it in the message box so you can change it first.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: Handing off to Wish Workshop
text:
Ask for several versions of a line and Genie may offer a **Wish Workshop** card
instead of a long list. **Open in Wish Workshop** opens it with those lines
selected and the wish already running. See [Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/).
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: Chime-ins (web)
text:
Now and then Genie offers a short nudge at a natural pause:

- when you come back to a song nobody has touched in a few weeks,
- when you have sat on an empty section for a while,
- when you have just finished a section.

It appears as a bubble beside the floating genie, or beside the Genie icon if
the floating genie is off. Nothing is sent until you click it, and then it opens
the chat with that question asked. Ignore it and it fades. You get at most one
in a browser session, and never while you are typing.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: The two Genie settings (web)
text:
Both are in **Settings**, under **Editor**, and both are on to begin with. On a
computer, open Settings from the avatar menu at the top right: the avatar menu →
**Settings**. In a phone browser it is the last tab in the bar along the bottom.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Floating Genie** | Shows the genie in the corner of the song editor. Genie stays in the right panel either way. |
| **Genie can chime in** | Allows the nudges above. |

You can also hide the floating genie from the editor itself: point at it and
click the small ×. Turn it back on from the avatar menu → **Settings**.

In a phone browser, the floating genie is how you open Genie. If you turn it
off, a Genie button appears at the top right of the song instead. Chime-ins
need the floating genie on a phone, since they have nowhere else to point.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: How Genie counts toward your plan
text:
On the free plan, each message to Genie uses one of your
{{limit.ai.freeCalls}} free AI calls, the same allowance the rest of the app
draws on.

Pro:
On Pro, Genie has a monthly allowance of its own, separate from the
{{limit.ai.proMonthly}} AI calls a month your other AI features use. Chatting
never eats into what Wish Workshop and the rest need. The allowance refills at
the start of each month.

A message Genie fails to answer is not counted. Send a lot in a row and it asks
you to wait a minute before the next one.

The numbers for the rest of the app are on [Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

heading: Guided Start (web)
text:
Guided Start is the [song wizard](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/song-wizard/) as a conversation with
Genie. It asks about the song you want to write, fills in the AI Context from
your answers, then offers titles and opening lines.

### Starting it

Click **New Song**. A blank song opens and asks how you want to start:

- **Guide me** opens Genie and begins the questions.
- **Start from scratch** gives you the blank page, and points out where Genie
  is in case you want it later.

On a song you have barely started, Genie also offers **Guide me through
starting this song** when you open the chat. It goes once the song has four
lyric lines, or once the mood, theme and similar artists are all filled in. It
is not offered on shared songs.

### The questions

Genie asks up to three questions, one at a time:

1. **What's the mood?** Pick up to three.
2. **What's the theme?** One sentence on what happens.
3. **Similar artists?** Pick up to two.

Each comes with suggestion chips. Click chips to fill the message box, type your
own answer, or mix the two, then click **Next**. **More ideas** deals a new set
of chips, and **Skip** moves on without an answer. Any question the AI Context
already answers is skipped.

The questions themselves cost nothing. Each answer goes straight into the
song's AI Context.

### Titles

Genie then brainstorms title ideas from your answers. Click one and then
**Next**, or type a title of your own. If the song already has a title of
yours, you can keep it.

**Brainstorm more titles** asks for another set. Free accounts can do this once
per Guided Start. **Skip titles** jumps to the end.

Picking a title sets it as the song's title. If the lyrics are empty, it also
lays down a section skeleton: Verse 1, Pre-chorus, Chorus and Verse 2.

### Lines

Last, Genie offers lines that go with the title. Click any to add it under
Verse 1. Click **Done** when you have what you want, or **Skip lines**.

Genie wraps up with a summary and reply chips such as **Help me write the
first verse**, and from there it is an ordinary Genie chat.

Pro:
The questions are free. The titles and lines come from one AI call, plus one
more if you brainstorm more titles, the same kind as [Spark](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/#creative-spark). If you are out of AI
calls, Guided Start skips that step and you carry on writing without it.
description: Talk a song through with Genie. It can see your lyrics, check rhymes and syllables, answer how-to questions about Lyric Genie, and suggest edits you apply with one tap.

text:
Stop typing for a moment and Lyric Genie offers a line where your cursor is. It
sits there in purple, and it is not part of your song until you tap it.

This is the one AI feature that comes to you rather than waiting to be asked.
description: A suggested next line appears at your cursor while you write. Tap to take it, or keep typing to ignore it.

heading: What you can do with it
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
| Action | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Tap the suggestion** | It becomes part of your lyrics at the cursor. |
| **Swipe sideways** | Shows the next suggestion, when there is more than one. |
| **Tap the cross** | Dismisses it. |
| **Keep typing** | It disappears on its own. |

Web app:
| Action | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Tab** or **click the suggestion** | It becomes part of your lyrics at the cursor. A click only counts a moment after the suggestion appears, so a stray click does not take it. |
| **Alt+Right**, **Alt+Left** | Shows the next or previous suggestion, when there is more than one. With a mouse, small arrows beside the suggestion do the same. On a touchscreen you swipe. |
| **Esc**, or click the cross | Dismisses it. |
| **Keep typing** | It disappears on its own. |

All the shortcuts are listed in [Keyboard shortcuts](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/).

It also goes away if you move the cursor, leave the editor, or a collaborator
edits the song. Nothing is inserted unless you tap.
description: A suggested next line appears at your cursor while you write. Tap to take it, or keep typing to ignore it.

heading: Turning it off
text:
**Preferences**, from the ⋯ menu in [the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/) or from
Settings, has the switch.

Web app:
On the web the switch is **In-line Suggestions** under Editor in Settings. It is
the same setting as the app's, so turning it off in one turns it off in the
other.

Plenty of writers turn it off. A suggestion that arrives while you are thinking
is either helpful or an interruption, and which one depends entirely on how you
work.
description: A suggested next line appears at your cursor while you write. Tap to take it, or keep typing to ignore it.

heading: It reads your settings
text:
Suggestions are not generic. Before writing one, the app reads:

- The song's **mood, theme and similar artists**, from
  [the editor's AI Context bar](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/).
- Your **[AI Style](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/ai-style/)** guidance and your list of words to
  avoid.

A song with no context gets noticeably blander suggestions, which is the same
rule that applies everywhere else in the app.
description: A suggested next line appears at your cursor while you write. Tap to take it, or keep typing to ignore it.

heading: If nothing ever appears
text:
On an account without AI access the feature is silent. It does not nag, it does
not show a paywall while you are writing, and nothing appears at the cursor.
The switch in Preferences is replaced by a row that says it needs AI access, and
tapping that row is what opens the upgrade screen.

That silence is deliberate. Interrupting someone mid-line to sell them something
would be the worst possible moment.

Pro:
In-line suggestions need AI access. See [Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: A suggested next line appears at your cursor while you write. Tap to take it, or keep typing to ignore it.

text:
A lyric sheet is a web page of your finished lyrics with the writer credits
underneath. You send someone a link and they read the song. No app, no account,
no file to open.

It is what you send a publisher, a collaborator's manager, or an artist you are
pitching to.
description: Turn a finished song into a shareable web page with proper writer credits.

heading: Making one
text:
From the ⋯ menu in [the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/), choose **Lyric Sheet**.

Web app:
On the web, click the **Lyric Sheet** button in the song bar (on a phone browser
it is in the top bar too). The same Create Lyric Sheet screen opens as a dialog
over the editor.
description: Turn a finished song into a shareable web page with proper writer credits.

heading: What your reader sees
text:
A title, the writers, and the lyrics with their section headings. It reads on a
phone or a laptop, and it is the same page whether you send it to a publisher
or to a friend.
description: Turn a finished song into a shareable web page with proper writer credits.

heading: Writer credits
text:
You are added as a writer automatically, with your legal name filled in from
your profile. Tap your name to open the rest of the fields.

| Field | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| **Legal Name** | Your name as it appears on a split sheet, not your artist name. |
| **Writer IPI #** | Your Interested Party Information number, the identifier your PRO knows you by. |
| **Publisher** | Your publisher, if you have one. |
| **Publisher IPI #** | Their number. |
| **PRO** | Your performing rights organisation: ASCAP, BMI, SESAC, SOCAN, PRS, APRA, or Other. |
| **Contact Email** | Where business enquiries should go. |

**Add Writer** adds a collaborator with the same set of fields.

Web app:
On the web, **PRO** is a drop-down. Choose **Other** to type the name of a
society that is not listed.

Fill these in once on your profile, under Settings, and every lyric sheet you
make from then on starts with them already filled.
description: Turn a finished song into a shareable web page with proper writer credits.

heading: After you create it
text:
The screen changes to show the finished sheet, with **Copy Link** and **Share
Link**. Copy Link flips to **Copied!** so you know it worked.

Web app:
On the web the link is also copied to your clipboard as soon as the sheet is
made. Each row under Previous Sheets has its own copy and delete buttons.

The link lives on `sheets.lyricgenie.app`, so it is obviously a Lyric Genie
page rather than an anonymous URL.

Every sheet you make is kept under **Previous Sheets** on this screen, so you
can find a link you sent last month without making a new one.
description: Turn a finished song into a shareable web page with proper writer credits.

heading: A sheet is frozen
text:
This is the part worth understanding. A lyric sheet is a **snapshot** of the
lyrics at the moment you created it. Keep writing and the sheet does not
change.

That is deliberate. A link you sent a publisher last week should still show
them what you sent, not whatever you happen to have typed since.

When you want to share the newer version, make a new sheet.
description: Turn a finished song into a shareable web page with proper writer credits.

heading: Taking a sheet down
text:
Delete a sheet from the Previous Sheets list and the link stops working for
everyone who has it. The app says as much before it does it.

Deleting a sheet cannot be undone, and anyone holding that link loses access
immediately. If you only want to share something newer, make a new sheet and
leave the old one alone.
description: Turn a finished song into a shareable web page with proper writer credits.

heading: On a shared song
text:
A song with collaborators gains a **Lyrics Version** picker at the top, so you can
choose whose words go on the sheet: the Master, your own tab, or a particular
collaborator's.

Lyric sheets are not a Pro feature. They are included on the free plan, along
with collaboration and recordings linked to lyrics.
description: Turn a finished song into a shareable web page with proper writer credits.

text:
A note is a comment pinned to particular words in the lyrics. Use one to flag a
line you are not sure about, ask a collaborator what they meant, or remind yourself
to come back to a rhyme.

Notes sit on top of the lyrics. They are never part of the text, so they don't
show up in a lyric sheet, in Perform, or in anything the AI reads.

Notes need iOS 2.22 or later in the iPhone app.
description: Highlight a word or a phrase in a song, leave a note on it, and talk it through with your collaborators in replies. Resolve a note when it's dealt with.

heading: Leaving a note
text:
Select the words the note is about: a word, a phrase or a few lines. Then:

iPhone and iPad app:
Tap **Note** in the bar of actions along the bottom of the editor.

Web app:
Open **⋯ More** on the floating toolbar and choose **Note**. In a phone browser
**Note** is in the row of buttons above the keyboard.

Type in **Add a note on these words…** and send it.

A note can be up to 1,000 characters.

You can leave a note on any tab: your own, a collaborator's, or the Master. It
belongs to the tab you left it on, so a note on a collaborator's chorus stays with
their chorus.
description: Highlight a word or a phrase in a song, leave a note on it, and talk it through with your collaborators in replies. Resolve a note when it's dealt with.

heading: Finding notes in the lyrics
text:
Noted words are underlined in the colour of the writer who left the note. A
small speech-bubble pin sits in the right margin, on the line where those words
end.

iPhone and iPad app:
Tap the pin to open the note. If several notes end on the same line, the pin
shows how many and opens a list of them.

Web app:
Click the pin, or put your cursor in the underlined words, and the note opens
beside them. Pointing at a pin lights up the words it is about. In a phone
browser the note opens as a sheet at the bottom of the screen.
description: Highlight a word or a phrase in a song, leave a note on it, and talk it through with your collaborators in replies. Resolve a note when it's dealt with.

heading: Replying
text:
Every note is a small thread. Type in **Reply…** and send. Everyone on the song
sees the note and every reply, with who wrote each one and when.

Web app:
Press `Enter` to send, and `Shift` `Enter` for a new line.
description: Highlight a word or a phrase in a song, leave a note on it, and talk it through with your collaborators in replies. Resolve a note when it's dealt with.

heading: Resolving a note
text:
When a note has been dealt with, click or tap **Resolve**. The underline and the
pin leave the lyrics, but the note is kept. **Reopen** brings it back.

Anyone on the song can resolve or reopen a note.
description: Highlight a word or a phrase in a song, leave a note on it, and talk it through with your collaborators in replies. Resolve a note when it's dealt with.

heading: Deleting a note
text:
The bin beside a note or a reply deletes it. You can delete what you wrote, and
the song's owner can delete anything. Deleting a note deletes its replies with
it, and it asks first.
description: Highlight a word or a phrase in a song, leave a note on it, and talk it through with your collaborators in replies. Resolve a note when it's dealt with.

heading: The list of notes
text:
Web app:
**Notes** is a section of the song panel on the left. It lists the open notes on
the tab you are looking at, with the resolved ones folded underneath. Click one
to jump to it and open it.

On a shared song, a line such as **2 notes on Sam →** points at other tabs with
open notes. Click it to switch to that tab.

iPhone and iPad app:
Choose **Notes** in the editor's ⋯ menu. It shows **Notes (2)** when the tab you
are on has open notes. The sheet lists them, with resolved ones folded under
**resolved**, and a line for each other tab that has open notes. Tap a note to
jump to it.
description: Highlight a word or a phrase in a song, leave a note on it, and talk it through with your collaborators in replies. Resolve a note when it's dealt with.

heading: Who sees notes
text:
On a shared song, everyone on the song sees every note. On a song only you
write, notes are yours alone.

Notes are not the same as the [collaborator chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/), which is a
conversation about the whole song. A note is about particular words.

[Search](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/search/) looks through notes and replies too, so you can find
a conversation about a line without remembering which song it was in.
description: Highlight a word or a phrase in a song, leave a note on it, and talk it through with your collaborators in replies. Resolve a note when it's dealt with.

text:
Perform puts your lyrics on a black screen in large type and gets everything
else out of the way. It is for the moment you stop writing and start singing.

Open it from the ⋯ menu in [the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/).

Web app:
On the web, click **Perform** in the song bar (on a phone browser it is in the
bar along the bottom). It covers the whole browser window, and **Esc** closes
it, as does the close button at the top right.
description: Full-screen scrolling lyrics on a black background, for singing your song rather than writing it.

heading: What it changes
text:
- **It fills the whole screen** (since iOS 2.22), with nothing of the app
  left around it.
- **The screen goes black** and stays dark whatever your phone is set to,
  because a bright screen in a dim room is the wrong thing to be looking at.
  On the web it is black whatever your browser's theme.
- **Your lyrics are white, your section headers are grey.** You can see where
  the chorus starts without reading the words.
- **The edges fade** rather than cutting off, so a line that is halfway on
  screen looks deliberate.
- **Nothing is editable.** You cannot change a word by accident with a
  microphone in your hand.
description: Full-screen scrolling lyrics on a black background, for singing your song rather than writing it.

heading: The font size slider
text:
The slider at the top runs between a small **A** and a large **A**. Drag it
until the words are readable from wherever your phone is propped.

iPhone and iPad app:
Your choice sticks per song, so a song you have already set up opens the way
you left it.

Web app:
The web slider is labelled **Text size** and runs from 16 to 48 pixels. It
starts at 30 each time you open Perform; the web does not remember it.
description: Full-screen scrolling lyrics on a black background, for singing your song rather than writing it.

heading: Greyed out in the menu
text:
**Perform** stays dimmed until the song has some lyrics. The web's button dims
the same way. There is nothing to
perform from an empty page, so the app does not offer it.
description: Full-screen scrolling lyrics on a black background, for singing your song rather than writing it.

heading: On a shared song
text:
A song with collaborators gets a picker at the top for choosing whose words to
sing.

| Option | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Master** | The agreed version of the song. |
| **My Lyrics** | Your own tab. |
| A collaborator's name | Their tab, with the song owner marked by a star. |

When the song has a Master, Perform opens on it by default, because the agreed
version is usually the one you want to sing. Your choice is remembered per
song.
description: Full-screen scrolling lyrics on a black background, for singing your song rather than writing it.

text:
A hummed melody is worth more than a description of one. The song editor lets
you record without leaving the page, and keeps the audio attached to the song
you were writing.

iPhone and iPad app:
The three audio buttons sit together in the grey capsule at the top of
[the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/).

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Recordings** | Opens the audio already attached to this song. |
| **Record** | Starts recording straight away. |
| **Freestyle** | Records and turns what you sang into lyrics. See [Freestyle](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/freestyle/). |

Web app:
On the web there is no button capsule. A **Recordings** section in the left panel
of [the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/) lists this song's audio, and its **Record** and
**Upload Audio** buttons add more. **Recordings** is also in the song bar's ⋯
menu, and opens that section. Freestyle is not on the web.
description: Capture audio while you write, attach it to the song, and tie a take to the exact lines it belongs to.

heading: The song's recordings
text:
This sheet shows only the audio belonging to the song you have open. Your full
library lives in the Recordings tab, which is a view across everything. See
[Recordings](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/).

Web app:
On the web this is the Recordings section of the left panel rather than a sheet.
Takes linked to lyrics come first. Playback happens in a small player pinned
below the editor, and each take's ⋯ menu has its transcript, rename, link and
archive options. While a new name is saving, a small spinner shows beside it.
**Upload Audio** adds a file from your computer.

On a shared song, **Send to Chat** in a take's ⋯ menu puts it in the
[collaborator chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/) message box, ready to send. On Pro,
**Download Original** saves an uploaded file exactly as it was. See
[Original files](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/#original-files).

When a notification tells you a collaborator added a recording, clicking it opens
the song with the Recordings section showing and that take highlighted.

Importing keeps a stereo file, such as a demo, in stereo and at a higher
quality. Takes you record in the app are mono.

A take recorded in a [session](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/) lands here too, named
for where it came from and when, such as **Session · Sam's mic · 5:54 PM**. A
recording of everyone is called **Session recording** and the time.

### The player

The player below the editor shows the take's name and who recorded it. On a
shared song, the play button and the waveform are in that writer's colour.

- **Click the waveform** to play from that point. Click the take that is
  playing to pause it.
- **The 🔗 button** appears when the take is linked to lyrics, and shows you
  those lines. See [below](#tying-a-take-to-particular-lines).
- **The volume slider**, on a computer, sets how loud it plays. The speaker
  button beside it mutes and unmutes.
description: Capture audio while you write, attach it to the song, and tie a take to the exact lines it belongs to.

heading: Recording while you write
text:
Tap **Record** and it starts immediately, because you tapped it with something
to sing. The sheet gives you a timecode, **Undo**, a pause button and **Save**.

Web app:
Click **Record** and a bar opens in the Recordings section with a live level
meter, a pause button and **Save**. Your browser asks for microphone access the
first time, and recording cannot start until you allow it. Pause and the meter
becomes the take so far, so you can play it back and scrub through it. Each
stretch between record and pause is kept separately, and **Backspace** drops the
last stretch, then the one before. Press **Enter** to save.

Takes are recorded in the browser and saved as AAC `.m4a` files, the same
format the app uses, so a take made on the web plays in the app. At the length
cap the web stops and saves what it has.

The timecode counts the audio you have actually captured. Pause stops the clock
with it, so the number always matches the length of the file rather than the
time you spent with the screen open.

Record first, tidy up later. A take you can hear beats a note that says
"something like a rising thing here".
description: Capture audio while you write, attach it to the song, and tie a take to the exact lines it belongs to.

heading: Tying a take to particular lines
text:
This is the part worth knowing about. A recording does not have to belong to
the whole song. It can belong to specific words.

Select the lines, then choose one of two things from the row of actions along
the bottom of the editor:

- **Record** starts a new recording anchored to those lines.
- **Link to Recording** attaches an existing take to them.

Web app:
On the web both are under **⋯ More** on the selection toolbar. A take shows the
words it is linked to underneath it, and the chip turns red with a broken link
if you later rewrite those lines so that the app can no longer find them.

Linked lines carry a marker in the left margin, in the colour of the writer who
made the take. Point at it and it says **Play**. Click it to play the take from
the start.

To find the lines a take belongs to, click its linked lyrics in the Recordings
section, the 🔗 button in the player, or **Show in song** on the
[Recordings page](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/recordings/). The song opens on the right tab, scrolls
to the lines, and flashes them so you can see which they are.

Linked lines can then be played back in order, so you can listen through a song
in the order you wrote it rather than the order you recorded it. See
[Selecting and editing lines](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/selecting/).

It also works the other way round. Start from a recording and the editor drops
into a picking mode, with a banner across the top reading **Select lyrics to
link**. Highlight the lines, tap **Link**, and the two are tied together. The
✕ on the banner backs out, which is the thing to reach for if you find yourself
in this mode and did not mean to be.

Web app:
On the web, open a take's ⋯ menu and choose **Link to Lyrics** (**Relink to
Lyrics** if it already has a link). The same banner appears. Select the lines,
and the toolbar over them shows just **Link**.
description: Capture audio while you write, attach it to the song, and tie a take to the exact lines it belongs to.

heading: Transcription
text:
Recordings with speech in them get transcribed, and the text turns up under the
recording with **Copy** and **Insert into Lyrics** beside it.

If a recording has nothing recognisable in it, you get **Transcription
unavailable** rather than a wrong guess.

Web app:
On the web a take that has a transcript shows it under **Transcript** in its ⋯
menu, with **Copy** and **Insert into Lyrics**. Takes without one show no
transcript option.
description: Capture audio while you write, attach it to the song, and tie a take to the exact lines it belongs to.

heading: Recordings made outside a song
text:
Audio captured from the Start tab, or with
[Record an Idea](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/siri-shortcuts/) from Siri or the Action Button, has
no song to belong to yet, so it lands in the Recordings tab as an unassigned
idea. Open it there and **Add to Song**
attaches it, or **New Song** creates one around it.

This is the thing people ask about most. A recording belongs to a song, not to
the tab you made it in. If you cannot find a take inside a song, it is almost
certainly sitting unassigned in the Recordings tab.
See [How it fits together](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/how-it-fits-together/).

Pro:
Recording length is capped by your plan: {{limit.recording.freePerItem}} per
recording on the free plan and {{limit.recording.proPerItem}} on Pro, with
{{limit.recording.freeTotal}} of storage free. Details on
[Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: Capture audio while you write, attach it to the song, and tie a take to the exact lines it belongs to.

text:
Most rhyming dictionaries take one word and give you words that rhyme with it.
Lyric Genie takes your phrase, works out which syllables carry the rhyme, and
then looks for words and phrases that match **both** of them.

That is the difference worth understanding before you use it. It is built for
internal and multisyllabic rhyme, not just the word at the end of the line.
description: The rhyme sheet in Lyric Genie finds multisyllabic rhymes for a whole phrase, not just the last word.

heading: Opening it
text:
Select a line or a word, then tap **Rhyme** in the row of actions along the
bottom of the editor. See [Selecting and editing lines](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/selecting/).

Web app:
Select a line or a word and click **Rhyme** on the selection toolbar. The rhymes
open in the **Rhymes** section of the right-hand panel, beside your lyrics,
and a button in the section expands it to full height with every column side by
side. On a phone browser it opens as a sheet, as in the app.

With nothing selected, the panel offers rhymes for the last word of the line
your cursor is on, and **Insert** puts the one you pick at your cursor.

The sheet works on one line or less. If Rhyme is greyed out, the selection is
too big.
description: The rhyme sheet in Lyric Genie finds multisyllabic rhymes for a whole phrase, not just the last word.

heading: The anchors
text:
Under your phrase is a row of chips, one per syllable, written the way they
sound rather than the way they are spelled. In "I love to sing" they read
*eye · luhv · too · sing*.

Two of them are highlighted. Those are the **anchors**, the syllables the app
thinks carry the rhyme. Everything else on the screen is built from them.

If it picked the wrong ones, tap the chip you want instead. A small **reset**
chip appears so you can put it back.
description: The rhyme sheet in Lyric Genie finds multisyllabic rhymes for a whole phrase, not just the last word.

heading: The columns
text:
Each tab across the middle is a different relationship between the two anchors,
and the number on it is how many results it found.

| Tab | What it finds |
| --- | --- |
| **A** | Rhymes for the first anchor on its own. |
| **B** | Rhymes for the second anchor on its own. |
| **A B** | Words containing both, adjacent, with no weak syllable between them. |
| **A · B** | Both, with one weak syllable between them. |
| **A · · B** | Both, with two or more syllables between them. |
| **Multi** | Longer phrases ending on the anchor. |

The combination tabs are the interesting ones. Asked for "love" and "sing"
adjacent, it returns single words that carry the whole rhyme, like *bluffing*
and *blushing*. Given a syllable of space it finds *abiding* and *accepting*.
description: The rhyme sheet in Lyric Genie finds multisyllabic rhymes for a whole phrase, not just the last word.

heading: How close a rhyme is
text:
Results are grouped into **Perfect** and **Near** within each column, so the
exact matches are at the top and the approximate ones below.

The **Slant** switch at the top widens the net further, letting in rhymes that
share a vowel shape without matching cleanly. Turn it off when you want only
the tight matches.
description: The rhyme sheet in Lyric Genie finds multisyllabic rhymes for a whole phrase, not just the last word.

heading: AI picks
text:
The sparkle badge at the top left counts the results the AI thought were worth
your attention, and those words are highlighted in the lists. Tap the badge to
filter the columns down to just those picks, and tap it again for the full list.

It is a way through a column of three thousand results. The ordering is a
suggestion, not a verdict, and the full list is still there underneath.

Web app:
Since web 0.8 the picks load by themselves, about three seconds after the
rhymes show, in the right-hand panel as well as the phone sheet. There is no
button to press.

Pro:
**The picks use quick AI calls**, the lighter allowance that in-line
suggestions also draw on. On the free plan you get them until your
{{limit.ai.freeCallsLowCost}} quick calls are used up. After that the picks
stop, and your other AI calls are left alone. The rhyme sheet itself is free,
and so is everything else on it. See
[Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: The rhyme sheet in Lyric Genie finds multisyllabic rhymes for a whole phrase, not just the last word.

heading: Trying it without the app
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
[RhymeGold](https://rhymegold.com) is a free web version of this rhyme sheet,
and it is the quickest way to get a feel for how the anchors and the columns
behave before you commit to a line. It runs the same engine over the same
dictionary: type a phrase and you get the same syllable anchors, the same
**Slant** switch, and the same combination columns with their counts.

The one thing it does not do is **AI picks**. Those read your song's mood, theme
and lyrics to decide what is worth your attention, and none of that exists on a
web page, so they stay in the app.

No sign-up, and it works on a desktop browser, which makes it handy for a
writing session where the phone is not the thing you are typing into.

Web app:
[RhymeGold](https://rhymegold.com) is a free, no-sign-up web version of this
rhyme sheet, handy when you only want to look up a phrase and not open a song.
description: The rhyme sheet in Lyric Genie finds multisyllabic rhymes for a whole phrase, not just the last word.

heading: Taking a word
text:
Tap a word to pick it, and the **Insert** button at the top right wakes up.
The chevron beside it opens the other options.

- **Insert at Top** and **Insert at Bottom** put it in without replacing
  anything.
- **Add to Scratchpad** parks it for later.
- **Copy** takes it out of the app.
description: The rhyme sheet in Lyric Genie finds multisyllabic rhymes for a whole phrase, not just the last word.

heading: Looking up more than one word
text:
You do not have to close the sheet to try something else. Tap the phrase at
the top and type a different word or phrase.

Pro:
Free accounts get {{limit.rhymes.freeDaily}} rhyme lookups a day, and Pro
removes the cap. A lookup is one distinct word per day, so going back to a word
you already looked up today is free and does not count again. Details on
[Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: The rhyme sheet in Lyric Genie finds multisyllabic rhymes for a whole phrase, not just the last word.

text:
One search box looks through everything you have in Lyric Genie: songs, the
lines inside them, notes, chat, recordings, ideas, concepts, projects and the
lyric sheets you have published. Type a word you remember and pick the result.
description: Find a song, a lyric line, a note, a chat message, a recording, a concept or a lyric sheet from anywhere in the Lyric Genie web app, with ⌘K or the search box on Home.
platformNote: Search across everything is in the web app. In the iPhone app, each tab has its own search field, and the Songs search also looks through lyrics.

heading: Opening search
text:
There are three ways in, and they search the same things.

- **Press `⌘` `K`** (`Ctrl` `K` on Windows and Linux) on any page, including
  inside a song.
- **Click the magnifying glass** in the app's top bar.
- **Type in the search box on [Home](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/home/)**, under the greeting.

`⌘` `K` and the magnifying glass open the command palette. It lists your results
first and then any commands that match, so the same box also runs actions like
"Perform" or switching between light and dark. See [Keyboard shortcuts](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/#finding-a-command).
description: Find a song, a lyric line, a note, a chat message, a recording, a concept or a lyric sheet from anywhere in the Lyric Genie web app, with ⌘K or the search box on Home.
platformNote: Search across everything is in the web app. In the iPhone app, each tab has its own search field, and the Songs search also looks through lyrics.

heading: What it searches
text:
| Group | What matches | Clicking a result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Songs** | The title, mood, theme and similar artists. | Opens the song. |
| **Lyrics** | A line of lyrics, on your tab, every collaborator's tab and the Master. | Opens the song on that tab, at that line. |
| **Notes** | The text of a [note](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/notes/) or a reply. | Opens the song with the note open. |
| **Chat** | A message in a song's [collaborator chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/). | Opens the song with the chat open, at that message. |
| **Recordings** | A take's name, or words in its transcript. | Opens the song and shows the take in its Recordings. |
| **Ideas** | A loose recording's name or transcript. | Opens the Recordings page, searched for it. |
| **Concepts** | The title, mood, theme and similar artists. | Opens Concepts with that card highlighted. |
| **Projects** | The project's name. | Opens Songs filtered to that project. |
| **Lyric sheets** | The song title, or a writer's name, on a [lyric sheet](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/) you published. | Opens the sheet in a new tab. |

Results come in that order, a handful from each group. Lyric sheets come last
because they are read-only pages, not something you edit. A lyrics result shows the
line itself and the song it is in, with **Master** added when the line is on the
Master tab.
description: Find a song, a lyric line, a note, a chat message, a recording, a concept or a lyric sheet from anywhere in the Lyric Genie web app, with ⌘K or the search box on Home.
platformNote: Search across everything is in the web app. In the iPhone app, each tab has its own search field, and the Songs search also looks through lyrics.

heading: How matching works
text:
- **Every word must match**, in any order. "rain window" finds a line with both
  words in it.
- **Case and accents don't matter.** "cafe" finds "Café", and "dont" finds
  "don't".
- **Titles that start with what you typed** come first, then the most recently
  changed.
- **Archived songs** are included, after the others, marked **Archived**.

Search runs in your browser on what is already loaded, so results appear as you
type. Notes and chat are read the first time you search in a visit, so they can
take a moment longer to appear than the rest.
description: Find a song, a lyric line, a note, a chat message, a recording, a concept or a lyric sheet from anywhere in the Lyric Genie web app, with ⌘K or the search box on Home.
platformNote: Search across everything is in the web app. In the iPhone app, each tab has its own search field, and the Songs search also looks through lyrics.

heading: Using the keyboard
text:
In either box, `↑` and `↓` move through the results, `Enter` opens the
highlighted one, and `Esc` closes the list. On Home, `Esc` also clears what you typed.
description: Find a song, a lyric line, a note, a chat message, a recording, a concept or a lyric sheet from anywhere in the Lyric Genie web app, with ⌘K or the search box on Home.
platformNote: Search across everything is in the web app. In the iPhone app, each tab has its own search field, and the Songs search also looks through lyrics.

text:
A section header is a line that names the part of the song underneath it.
Lyric Genie picks them out, sets them in purple, and then uses them everywhere
else.

Naming your sections is optional, and it is the cheapest thing you can do to
make the rest of the app work properly.
description: How to name a verse, chorus or bridge in Lyric Genie, and what the app does once it knows.

heading: Making one
text:
Type the name of a section on its own line. That is the whole technique.

Web app:
Shorthand is converted when you press Enter at the end of the header line.

Brackets are optional. The app strips them, so `[Chorus]`, `(Chorus)`,
`**Chorus**` and plain `Chorus` all end up the same. Paste in lyrics from
somewhere else and the headers usually survive the trip.
description: How to name a verse, chorus or bridge in Lyric Genie, and what the app does once it knows.

heading: Shorthand
text:
You do not have to type the whole word.

| What you type | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| `V1`, `V2` | Verse 1, Verse 2 |
| `PC`, `pre`, `prechorus`, `pre chorus` | Pre-Chorus |
| `HK` | Hook |
| `post`, `postchorus` | Post-Chorus |

Repeated sections are numbered for you as the song grows, so a second verse
becomes Verse 2 without you counting.
description: How to name a verse, chorus or bridge in Lyric Genie, and what the app does once it knows.

heading: Changing a section's type
text:
Web app:
The web has no button for changing a header's type. A header is just a line of
text, so to change a Verse into a Chorus, retype the line. The shorthand above
works here too.

To move a whole section, use the **Sections** list in the left panel. It shows
every header with the first line under it. Click one to jump to it, or drag one
to a new place to move the header and all its lines in one edit. Undo takes it
back.

The expand button on the **Sections** heading, or its icon on the left edge of
the window, opens a bigger view that shows every line of each section. Drag a
section there to move it, lines and all. On a shared song the heading says
whose tab you are looking at: **You**, **Master** or a collaborator's name.

iPhone and iPad app:
Put your cursor anywhere on a header and a button appears at the right of that
line. Tap it to swap the section for another type.

The eight types, in the order the app lists them:

| Type | What it usually is |
| --- | --- |
| **Intro** | The way in. |
| **Verse** | The story, with the details that change each time. |
| **Pre-Chorus** | The lift that sets up the chorus. |
| **Chorus** | The hook and the main idea. |
| **Hook** | The chorus's counterpart in hip-hop. |
| **Post-Chorus** | The tag that lands after the chorus. |
| **Bridge** | The contrast, usually once, late. |
| **Outro** | The way out. |
description: How to name a verse, chorus or bridge in Lyric Genie, and what the app does once it knows.

heading: Why bother
text:
Sections are not decoration. Four parts of the app read them.

- **[Arrange mode](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/arrange-mode/)** lets you select a header and take
  every line under it, which is how you move a whole chorus in one go.
- **[Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/)** greys the headers and leaves your lyrics white, so
  you can see the shape of the song while you sing it.
- **Lyric sheets** keep the structure when you share the song.
- **The Master tab** on a shared song files incoming lines by section, and
  orders them properly rather than in the order they arrived.

If you only ever name one thing, name the choruses. That is what makes
Arrange mode and the Master tab useful.
description: How to name a verse, chorus or bridge in Lyric Genie, and what the app does once it knows.

text:
Selecting text is how you point a tool at a particular line. Nothing in the
editor works on your selection until you make one, and what the app offers back
depends on how much you picked.

iPhone and iPad app:
Select some text and the bar along the bottom of the editor turns into a row of
actions for that selection. Since iOS 2.22 every tool is in that one row. The
menu on the selection itself keeps only the system's own Cut, Copy and Paste.

Web app:
On the web there is one bar. Select text and a floating toolbar
appears just above the selection, holding every tool described below. On a
phone browser the same buttons sit in a row docked above the keyboard, and
the less-used ones sit in that row instead of under **More**.
description: Select a lyric and the editor offers rhymes, synonyms, syllable changes and a rewrite. What appears depends on how much you selected.

heading: The selection bar
text:
Web app:
The floating toolbar holds, left to right:

| Button | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Rewrite** | Hands the selection to [Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/) to change. | The selection is six lines or less, on a tab you can edit. |
