| **To Master** | Sends the selected lines to the Master tab. See [The Master](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/master/). | The song is shared, and you are not on the Master tab. |
| **To Me** | Adds the selected lines to the end of your own tab. | You are looking at a collaborator's tab or the Master. |
| **Send to…** | Sends the selected lines to a collaborator, who gets them in the song's chat. See [Sending lines](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sending/). | The song is shared. |
| **Ask Genie** | Opens [Genie](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/) with the selection attached. | There is a selection. |
| **Rhyme** | Opens the rhyme tool for what you selected. | The selection is one line or less. |
| **Thesaurus** | Opens synonyms and related words. | The selection is one line or less. |
| **⋯ More** | Note, Make Blank, Move to Scratchpad, Record, Link to Recording. In the Scratchpad it also offers Move to Lyrics. | Each item appears when it applies. |
| **−2 −1 +1 +2** | Rewrites the line with fewer or more syllables. See [Syllables](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/syllables/). | The selection is a single line on a tab you can edit. +1 needs a syllable to start from, −1 needs two, −2 needs three. |

To Master, To Me and Send to… send whole lines, widening your selection to the line
starts and ends, the same as Arrange mode does.

Rhyme and Thesaurus open in the right-hand panel next to your lyrics rather
than over them.

iPhone and iPad app:
The row reads left to right, and scrolls sideways when it is longer than the
screen. **Done**, pinned at the right, puts the keyboard away.

| Button | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Rewrite** | Hands the selection to [Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/) to change. | Your own tab. Up to six lines. |
| **Rhyme** | Opens the [rhyme sheet](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/rhymes/) for what you selected. | The selection is one line or less. |
| **Thesaurus** | Opens synonyms and related words. | The selection is one line or less. |
| **Sounds Like** | Words that sound like the selection. | Three words or fewer. |
| **Word Associations** | Words that go with it. | Three words or fewer. |
| **+1 Syllable**, **-1 Syllable** | Rewrites the line one syllable longer or shorter. See [Syllables](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/syllables/). | A single line on your own tab. -1 needs two syllables. |
| **Make Blank** | Swaps the words for a [blank](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/blanks/) of the same length. | A single line on your own tab. |
| **Move to Scratchpad** | Cuts the selection out of the lyrics into [the Scratchpad](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/). | Your own tab. |
| **Note** | Leaves a [note](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/notes/) on the words. | Any tab. |
| **Record** | Starts a recording anchored to these lines. | Your own tab. |
| **Link to Recording** | Ties an existing take to these words. | Any tab but the Master. |
| **Save to Concepts** | Files the selection as a [concept](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/concepts/). | Always. |
| **Arrange Lines** | Opens [Arrange mode](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/arrange-mode/) with these lines ticked. | Always. |
| **To Master** | Sends the lines to the Master. See [The Master](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/master/). | A shared song. |
| **To Me** | Adds the lines to the end of your own tab. | A collaborator's tab or the Master. |
| **To Collaborator…** | Sends the lines to a collaborator, who gets them in the song's chat. See [Sending lines](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sending/). | Your own tab on a shared song. |
| **Genie** | Opens [Genie](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/) with the selection attached. | Any tab. |

To Master, To Me and To Collaborator… send whole lines, widening your
selection to the line starts and ends.

On a collaborator's tab or the Master the row keeps only what reads or sends:
lookups, notes, sends and Genie. Anything that would change their words is
left off. Since iOS 2.23 the bar also appears there; before, it only showed
on your own tab.

If **Sounds Like** and **Word Associations** are missing, you selected more than
three words. Shorten the selection and they come back.
description: Select a lyric and the editor offers rhymes, synonyms, syllable changes and a rewrite. What appears depends on how much you selected.

heading: Why the buttons go grey
text:
Rhyme and Thesaurus do not disappear when the selection is too long. They dim,
so you can see what you are missing. The other actions are left off the row
when they do not apply.

Web app:
Rewrite, Rhyme and Thesaurus dim on the web too. To Master, To Me and the
syllable buttons are different: they are left off the bar when they do not
apply.

If you ask for a rewrite on more than the app can handle, it tells you rather
than sending it. The cap is six lines and 500 characters. For a long verse,
work through it a few lines at a time.
description: Select a lyric and the editor offers rhymes, synonyms, syllable changes and a rewrite. What appears depends on how much you selected.

heading: The menu on the selection
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Long-press a selection and you get the system's own menu: Cut, Copy, Paste and
Select All. Everything else that used to be in this menu moved to the bar
along the bottom in iOS 2.22.

**Record** and **Link to Recording** are the two people miss. They tie audio to
specific words rather than to the song as a whole, so you can play back the
take that belongs to a particular line. See [Recordings](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/).

Web app:
The web has no separate menu on the selection. Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All
are your browser's own, from the right-click menu or the keyboard. The extra
tools are in the floating toolbar's **⋯ More** menu:

| Item | When it appears |
| --- | --- |
| **Note** | Leaves a note on the selected words for everyone on the song. See [Notes on lyrics](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/notes/). |
| **Make Blank** | You can edit this tab, and the selection can be turned into a blank. |
| **Move to Scratchpad** | You can edit this tab. Cuts the selection out of the lyrics into [the Scratchpad](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/). |
| **Record** | You can edit this tab. Starts a recording anchored to this line. |
| **Link to Recording** | You can edit this tab and the song has a take to link. |
| **Move to Lyrics** | You are in the Scratchpad. Moves the selection to the end of your lyrics. |

**Sounds Like**, **Word Associations** and **Save to Concepts** from the app's
menu are not on the web selection toolbar.
description: Select a lyric and the editor offers rhymes, synonyms, syllable changes and a rewrite. What appears depends on how much you selected.

heading: Moving whole lines instead
text:
Everything above edits text. When you want to reorder, duplicate or delete
whole lines rather than rewrite them, use Arrange mode: **Arrange** at the left
of the bar along the bottom of [the editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/), or **Arrange Lines** on
a selection.

Web app:
On the web it is the **Arrange** pill in the song bar.

The difference is worth holding on to. Selecting text points a writing tool at
your words. Arrange mode moves your words around without changing them.
description: Select a lyric and the editor offers rhymes, synonyms, syllable changes and a rewrite. What appears depends on how much you selected.

text:
Sometimes a line says the right thing and does not fit the tune. It is a
syllable short, or a syllable too long, and no amount of staring fixes it.

The syllable tool rewrites the line to the length you need and keeps the
meaning.
description: Make a line one or two syllables longer or shorter without losing what it says.

heading: Opening it
text:
Select a single line and tap **+1 Syllable** or **-1 Syllable** in the row of
actions along the bottom of the editor. See
[Selecting and editing lines](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/selecting/).

Web app:
Select a single line and use the **−2 −1 +1 +2** group on the selection
toolbar. The panel's **Syllables** section has −1 and +1 as well. The line has
to be on a tab you can edit. The rewrites open in a side sheet next to your
lyrics, on the tab for the change you picked.

Both only appear for a single-line selection, and **-1 Syllable** needs a line
with at least two syllables to take one away from.
description: Make a line one or two syllables longer or shorter without losing what it says.

heading: Choosing how far to go
text:
You arrive on the option you picked, and the four tabs let you change your mind
without starting again.

| Tab | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **-2** | Removes two syllables. |
| **-1** | Removes one. |
| **+1** | Adds one. |
| **+2** | Adds two. |
description: Make a line one or two syllables longer or shorter without losing what it says.

heading: Reading the results
text:
Web app:
On the web, each suggestion shows its own syllable count in small type beside
it, so you can see it landed where you asked. The meaning score and the change
badge described below are in the app.

Every suggestion carries two things.

**A score**, which is how well the rewrite held on to your original meaning.
It is coloured, so a green result kept the sense and a red one took liberties
with it. High scores tend to be small additions like *I love to sing out*.
Lower ones rearrange more, like *I love singing songs*.

**A badge** showing the change it actually achieved, so you can see it did what
you asked rather than drifting to a different length.

Do not assume the top result is the one you want. A lower score often means a
more interesting line, and the score only measures faithfulness to what you
already wrote.
description: Make a line one or two syllables longer or shorter without losing what it says.

heading: Changing the line
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
The pencil next to the phrase at the top lets you edit the words and ask again,
without closing the sheet and reselecting. Useful when the first answer shows
you the line was slightly wrong to begin with.

Web app:
The web sheet has no pencil. To try different words, close the sheet, edit the
line and ask again.
description: Make a line one or two syllables longer or shorter without losing what it says.

heading: Taking one
text:
Tap a suggestion to pick it, and **Insert** wakes up. The chevron beside it
offers **Insert at Cursor**, **Insert at Top**, **Insert at Bottom**, **Add to
Scratchpad** and **Copy**.

Web app:
On the web every suggestion has its own **Insert** button, with a menu of the
other options beside it.

Pro:
Syllable control needs AI access, so it is a Pro feature. See
[Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: Make a line one or two syllables longer or shorter without losing what it says.

text:
The **View** menu changes how your lyrics look without changing the lyrics.
It has three options, and all three start off.

| Option | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Rhyme colors** | Words that rhyme with each other, in matching colours. |
| **Syllable counts** | Each line's syllable count, in the left margin. |
| **Rhyme scheme** | Each line's rhyme letter (A, B, C…), in the right margin. |

You can turn on any mix of them. The **View** button is highlighted while any
of them is on, so you can tell at a glance.
description: Colour the rhymes in your lyrics, and show each line's syllable count and rhyme-scheme letter in the margins of the Lyric Genie web editor.

heading: Where the menu is
text:
On a computer, **View** is in the song bar along the top of the song, next to
**Wish** or **Spark**. In a phone browser it is the last button in the bar
along the bottom. See [The desktop workspace](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/workspace/).

Click an option to tick or untick it. The menu stays open, so you can try them
one after another.

The menu hides while [Arrange mode](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/arrange-mode/) is on.
description: Colour the rhymes in your lyrics, and show each line's syllable count and rhyme-scheme letter in the margins of the Lyric Genie web editor.

heading: Rhyme colors
text:
Words that rhyme get a tint and an underline in a shared colour, so a rhyme
running through a verse shows up as a pattern.

It judges rhymes the way a listener would hear them, within each stanza:

- **Line endings** count when they are Perfect or Near rhymes, as the
  [rhyme engine](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/rhymes/#how-close-a-rhyme-is) judges them, and no more
  than two lines apart.
- **Words inside lines** only count as Perfect rhymes, on the same line or the
  next.

A stanza here is a run of lines with no blank line between them. Section
headers, very short words and the most common little words are left out, and it
takes two different words to make a rhyme. Slant rhymes are never coloured.

Rhyme colours are off each time you open a song.
description: Colour the rhymes in your lyrics, and show each line's syllable count and rhyme-scheme letter in the margins of the Lyric Genie web editor.

heading: Syllable counts
text:
A small number in the left margin of every lyric line gives its syllable count.
It updates as you type. Section headers and empty lines get no number, and a
blank counts as the syllables it stands for.

The number is the line's usual spoken count. Words that can be sung shorter or
longer still count once. To change a line's length, see
[Syllables](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/syllables/).
description: Colour the rhymes in your lyrics, and show each line's syllable count and rhyme-scheme letter in the margins of the Lyric Genie web editor.

heading: Rhyme scheme
text:
A letter in the right margin of each line shows which lines rhyme. The first
ending in a stanza is **A**, the next one that does not rhyme with it is **B**,
and so on. A line whose ending rhymes with an earlier one takes its letter.

- Letters start again at **A** in each stanza.
- A line that only slant-rhymes an earlier group gets that letter with a mark,
  like **A′**.
- A line that ends in a blank gets no letter.

The letters come from the same rhyme engine as the rhyme colours, so they
settle a moment after you stop typing rather than on every key. With **Rhyme
colors** on as well, each letter takes the colour of the rhyme it stands for,
so the margin and the words match.
description: Colour the rhymes in your lyrics, and show each line's syllable count and rhyme-scheme letter in the margins of the Lyric Genie web editor.

heading: Good to know
text:
- The margins are remembered by this browser, for every song. Rhyme colours are
  not.
- Margin numbers and letters are not part of the lyrics. They cannot be
  selected and are not copied or shared.
- All three work on a collaborator's tab and the Master too, since they only read
  the lyrics.
- None of them use AI or count toward your plan.
description: Colour the rhymes in your lyrics, and show each line's syllable count and rhyme-scheme letter in the margins of the Lyric Genie web editor.

text:
Wish Workshop is the main AI writing tool in [the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/). It
helps you rewrite a line, or find new material when you are stuck.

It does two quite different jobs, and which one you get depends entirely on
whether you selected any text first. That is the single thing to understand
about it.

iPhone and iPad app:
Open it from the bar along the bottom of the editor. With nothing selected,
tap **Wish**, the lamp. With text selected, tap **Rewrite**, the first button
in the row. Before iOS 2.22 the lamp floated at the bottom right instead.

Web app:
Click **Wish** in the song bar, or **Rewrite** on
the selection toolbar. Wish Workshop opens in the right-hand panel next to your
lyrics, so the song stays in view while you work. The panel's header has a
back arrow instead of a close button, and a button to widen it. On a phone
browser it opens as a bottom sheet. The button reads **Spark** when nothing is
selected.
description: The AI writing tool in the song editor. What it does to a line you selected, and what it does when you select nothing.

heading: Two ways in
text:
**Select a line first** and Wish Workshop works on that line. Your selection
appears as a purple bubble at the top, the action button reads **Replace**, and
a row of one-tap wishes lights up along the bottom. On the web the selection
sits in the panel the same way, and the layout is the same.

**Select nothing** and you get Creative Spark instead, which generates new
material rather than changing anything you wrote. The action button reads
**Insert**, and the one-tap wishes are greyed out, because there is nothing for
them to act on.

Web app:
The four Creative Spark options appear as tiles. The right panel shows the
same tiles whenever nothing is selected, so you can start a Spark without
opening Wish Workshop first.
description: The AI writing tool in the song editor. What it does to a line you selected, and what it does when you select nothing.

heading: It asks for context first
text:
The first time you open it on a song with no [AI Context](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/), Wish
Workshop stops and asks for some before it will do anything.

You can tap **Continue Anyway** and skip it. It is worth a minute of your time
instead. These three fields are what the AI reads to work out what your song is
supposed to sound like, and the difference between a filled-in song and an
empty one is not subtle.

**Theme** does the most work of the three, and it rewards being specific. The
app's own example is a good model: "she leaves the town that made her small"
will get you further than "leaving home".

Whatever you enter here is saved to the song, so you are asked once, not every
time.

Web app:
On the web it doesn't stop you. Wish Workshop runs straight away, and the
song's **AI Context** fields open in the left panel beside it, with a note
saying better context gets better results. Fill them in there and the next wish
uses them. (On a phone-sized window, where only one panel fits, it skips this.)
description: The AI writing tool in the song editor. What it does to a line you selected, and what it does when you select nothing.

heading: Rewriting a line
text:
With a line selected, you have three ways to ask for a change.

**Tap a wish.** The row along the bottom starts with **Rewrite**, **Tweak**,
**Happier** and **Darker**, and scrolls sideways to around thirty more. They
range from tonal (More Vulnerable, More Sarcastic, More Nostalgic) to technical
(Make It Rhyme, Easier to Sing, More Alliteration).

**Describe what you want.** The field at the bottom reads *or describe your
wish...* and takes plain English. Use it when none of the chips is quite the
thing.

**Set the constraints first.** Two toggles sit above the chips, and both are
**on** by default.

| Toggle | What it protects |
| --- | --- |
| **Keep end rhyme** | The rhyme at the end of the line survives the rewrite. On a multi-line selection this becomes **Keep rhyme scheme**. |
| **Keep meter/syllables** | The new line is singable to the same melody as the old one. |

Those defaults are the right ones most of the time. Turn them off when you want
a genuinely free rewrite and you are willing to re-fit the melody.

A selection can be up to six lines and 500 characters. Ask for more than that
and the app tells you so rather than sending it. If you need a whole verse
rewritten, do it a few lines at a time.
description: The AI writing tool in the song editor. What it does to a line you selected, and what it does when you select nothing.

heading: Lines with blanks
text:
Select a line that has a [blank](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/blanks/) in it and Wish Workshop fills
the blank instead of rewriting the line. Your own words stay as they are, and
each result fits the blank's syllable count. When the blank ends the line, the
rhyme switch reads **Rhyme with** and the word it should rhyme with; tap the
word to pick another.
description: The AI writing tool in the song editor. What it does to a line you selected, and what it does when you select nothing.

heading: Reading a result
text:
A wish comes back as a stack of options, not one answer.

Three things on this screen are easy to miss.

- **Load More** asks for another batch without spending a new wish on a
  reworded prompt.
- **The dots at the bottom** mean there is more than one page of results.
  Swipe sideways, or use the chevrons at the edges, to move between them.
- **The eye button** previews the selected line in place, in your lyrics, so
  you can see it in context before you commit to it.

Web app:
On the web there is no eye button, because the preview is always on. While
Wish Workshop is open, the words it is working on get a moving dashed underline
in your lyrics, and the result you pick stands in their place, pulsing, until
you press **Replace**. Pick your original line and the underline comes back.
Use the chevrons to move between pages of results. The row of wishes scrolls
sideways, with arrows at either end when there are more.

**Keyboard.** Up and Down move through the results, starting with your
original line. Enter runs the default action on the highlighted result. Esc
steps back out of the panel. Esc and Enter are ignored while the cursor is in a
text field, so typing a wish is safe.

The greyed line is the one you chose and the coloured line under it is the next
option. Swipe sideways to walk through them in place, which is a better way to
judge a line than reading it on the results screen. On the web, turn on
**Preview** and use the chevrons.
description: The AI writing tool in the song editor. What it does to a line you selected, and what it does when you select nothing.

heading: Taking the result
text:
Nothing changes in your song until you say so. The button at the top right
applies the result, and the chevron beside it opens the other options.

- **Replace Selection** puts the new line where the old one was.
- **Insert at Top** and **Insert at Bottom** add it without removing anything.
- **Replace Title** swaps the song title instead, for a title wish.
- **Add to Scratchpad** parks it in [the Scratchpad](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/) to decide later.
- **Copy to Clipboard** takes it out of the app.

Web app:
The main button runs the default action for the kind of wish you are in, and
Enter does the same. Pick a different action from the menu beside it and it
runs, and it becomes the default for that kind of wish (a rewrite, a Spark, a
title). The choice is remembered in this browser, not on your account. Wish
Workshop stays open after an action, so you can try another result straight
away. The option is labelled **Copy** on the web.

If a result is close but not right, ask again from the same screen. The workshop
keeps iterating on the same thread rather than starting over.
description: The AI writing tool in the song editor. What it does to a line you selected, and what it does when you select nothing.

heading: Creative Spark
text:
With nothing selected, you get four options.

| Option | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| **Spark Sections** | A complete verse, chorus, bridge or pre-chorus. |
| **Spark Titles** | Song title ideas. |
| **Spark Phrases** | Phrases and hooks, not finished lines. |
| **Spark Lines** | Complete lyrical lines. |

Spark Phrases is the one people underuse. A hook you can build a chorus around
is often more useful than a finished chorus you did not write.
description: The AI writing tool in the song editor. What it does to a line you selected, and what it does when you select nothing.

heading: History
text:
**History**, at the bottom right of the sheet, keeps every wish session for
this song. Tap one to reload it, including the results you did not take.

It is per song, so a session you are looking for is in the song it belongs to,
not in one long global list. Each entry says how many iterations it holds, and
**Load More** pages further back.

Sessions accumulate. Swipe one away to delete just that thread, which asks
first, or use **Clear All** to empty the song's history. A song with no history
yet says **Nothing to revisit yet**.

On the web, History is kept in this browser, and the app keeps its own on each
device, so sessions never carry across. To delete one thread on the web, use
the bin button on its row instead of swiping.
description: The AI writing tool in the song editor. What it does to a line you selected, and what it does when you select nothing.

heading: When it will not run
text:
Two different things can stop it, and they look different.

**It asks for more to work with.** If the song has neither context nor a title,
the workshop says so instead of guessing. Fill in a couple of the context
fields and try again.

**It asks you to upgrade.** Wish Workshop needs AI access. Free accounts get a
small number of AI calls to try it with, and the upgrade screen appears when
those run out.

Pro:
Wish Workshop is a Pro feature. The free plan includes a handful of AI calls
so you can see what it does, and Pro raises that to
{{limit.ai.proMonthly}} a month. The exact numbers are on
[Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: The AI writing tool in the song editor. What it does to a line you selected, and what it does when you select nothing.

text:
On the web, a song opens as a workspace that fills the window. Your lyrics sit
in the middle as a page. What the song contains is on the left. Tools for the
line you are working on are on the right.

You can write with both side panels shut. They are there for when you want
them, and every one of them remembers how you left it.
description: The three panels of the Lyric Genie web editor, how to resize and hide them, and what changes in a phone browser.

heading: The song bar
text:
The row along the top of the song belongs to the song, not the app.

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Songs** | Back to your song list. |
| **Undo**, **Redo** | One history for the whole page: lyrics, title and AI Context. |
| **Wish** or **Spark** | Opens [Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/). It reads **Wish** with lyrics selected and **Spark** without. |
| **View** | Rhyme colours and the margins. See [Rhyme colors and margins](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/view-options/). On a shared song it also has **Side by side**. See [Side by side](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/tabs/#side-by-side-web-app-only). |
| **Arrange** | See [Arrange mode](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/arrange-mode/). |
| **Blank** | Adds a one-syllable blank at the cursor, or one more syllable to the blank already there. |
| **Record** | Starts a take straight away. With lyrics selected, the take is linked to those lines. See [Recordings](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/recordings/). |
| Save state | Whether your last change has reached the cloud. |
| Scratchpad | Opens and closes the scratchpad drawer. |
| Collaborators | The faces of who is on the song. Click to open Collaborators in the left panel. |
| **Perform** | See [Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/). |
| **Lyric Sheet** | Makes a [lyric sheet](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/) to share. |
| More | **Recordings**, **Keyboard shortcuts**, **Archive**, and **Delete** for a song only you write (**Stop Sharing & Delete** for a shared one nobody has joined yet). |

The app's own bar, with the logo and the main pages, sits above all this. The
up arrow at its right hides it to give the song more room. The genie logo that
then appears at the start of the song bar brings it back.
description: The three panels of the Lyric Genie web editor, how to resize and hide them, and what changes in a phone browser.

heading: The left panel: the song
text:
Everything the song is made of, in collapsible sections. Click a section's
heading to fold it away.

- **AI Context.** The song's mood, theme and similar artists, which every AI
  feature reads. Press **Enter** to finish a field. See
  [AI Style](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/ai-style/) for the instructions that apply to all your
  songs instead.
- **Recordings.** The takes on this song, with **Record** and **Import** at the
  top once there is at least one. See
  [Recordings in a song](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/recordings/).
- **Sections.** Every section header in the lyrics, with its first line. Click
  one to jump to it. The one your cursor is in is highlighted. On a shared song
  the heading says whose tab the list is for: **You**, **Master** or a
  collaborator's name.
- **Notes.** The notes left on the tab you are looking at. Click one to jump to
  it. See [Notes on lyrics](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/notes/).
- **Collaborators.** Who is on the song and what each of them is doing right
  now. On a shared song this section comes first. See
  [Collaborator tabs](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/tabs/).
- **Session.** On a shared song, where you can, a live video and voice session
  with your collaborators. During a session, the **Room view** button in this
  section's header, beside Expand, lets the session fill the page for you:
  video, Collaborators, Recordings and Chat. **Lyrics** takes you back, and
  lights up if the lyrics changed while you were in the room. See
  [Sessions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/).
- **Chat.** On a shared song, a chat with your collaborators, near
  Collaborators. See [Collaborator chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/).

### Putting the sections in your order

On a computer, drag a section's heading up or down to move it within the panel.
The same works for the sections of the right panel. The order you choose is
kept for every song in that browser.

The expand button on a section's heading opens that section on its own, filling
the panel. An expanded left panel can be dragged wider, up to 1400 pixels,
always leaving room for the lyrics.

### Moving a whole section

Drag a section in the **Sections** list to move it, header, lines and all, to a
new place in the song. It is one change, so a single **Undo** puts it back.

For more room, expand **Sections**, with the button on its heading or its icon
on the left edge of the window. The expanded view shows every line of each
section, so you can see what you are moving, and you drag a whole section the
same way.

Sections only move on your own tab. On a collaborator's tab, or while
[Arrange mode](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/arrange-mode/) is on, the list still jumps but does not
drag.
description: The three panels of the Lyric Genie web editor, how to resize and hide them, and what changes in a phone browser.

heading: The right panel: tools and Genie
text:
The right panel shows either the writing tools or Genie, chosen from the column
of icons along the right edge of the window.

| Icon | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| Panel button, at the top | Shows or hides the panel. Opening it shows the writing tools. |
| **Rhymes** | Rhymes for the selection, on their own. |
| **Thesaurus** | Synonyms for the selection, on their own. |
| **Syllables** | The syllable tools for the selection, on their own. |
| **Wish Workshop** | [Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/), widened. |
| **Genie**, at the bottom | The [Genie chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/) for this song. |

The highlighted icon is the one showing. Click it again to close the panel.
Rhymes, Thesaurus and Syllables follow the order you have put the right panel's
sections in.

### Writing tools

The tools follow your selection. Select a word or a line and the panel fills
with things to do with it, and it keeps them after you click away, so you can
try one rhyme, then another. The × beside the selected text clears it.

With something selected:

- **Rhymes**, from the same engine as the [rhyme sheet](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/rhymes/). They
  load on their own, since they cost nothing.
- **Wish Workshop**, to rewrite up to six selected lines.
- **Thesaurus**, which uses AI, so it waits for you to ask.
- **Syllables**, the line's count and an AI rewrite one syllable longer or
  shorter. See [Syllables](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/syllables/).

With nothing selected:

- **Spark**, to brainstorm sections, titles, phrases or lines at your cursor.
- **Rhymes** for the last word of the line your cursor is on, which is usually
  the word you are trying to rhyme.

**This song**, at the bottom, counts sections, lines and words either way.

### Giving a tool more room

The expand button on **Rhymes** or **Thesaurus** opens that tool on its own and
widens the panel. The widen button in a tool's header switches between wide and
normal. Wide folds the left panel away to make room, and Wish Workshop
remembers which you used last.

The back arrow, or **Esc**, returns to the full list of tools.
description: The three panels of the Lyric Genie web editor, how to resize and hide them, and what changes in a phone browser.

heading: Resizing and hiding the panels
text:
- **Drag the inner edge** of either panel to make it wider or narrower. The
  edge has a small double-line grip in the middle so you can find it.
- **Double-click that edge** to put the panel back to its normal width.
- **Drag it most of the way closed** and it folds down to a slim column of
  icons.

The lyrics keep a sensible minimum width, so a panel stops growing before it
squeezes the page.

On a computer both columns of icons stay put whether or not their panel is
open. The left one has the panel button, then **Collaborators**, **AI Context**,
**Chat** and **Session** (on a shared song), **Sections** and **Recordings**,
each of which opens that section on its own. They follow the order you have put
the left panel's sections in. A red dot on the Chat icon means there are
messages you have not read. The icon
for whatever is showing is highlighted, and clicking it again closes it. With
the left panel folded, you can also drag the column's edge outward to open it.

On a very wide screen the lyrics stop at a comfortable reading width and sit in
the middle of the space, rather than stretching across it.

Lyric Genie remembers which panels were open and how wide they were, per
browser. On a shared song it also remembers which tab you were on, so the song
reopens there. The first time you open a song, the left panel shows on a window at
least 1024 pixels wide and the right on one at least 1280.
description: The three panels of the Lyric Genie web editor, how to resize and hide them, and what changes in a phone browser.

heading: The scratchpad
text:
The scratchpad is a drawer under the page for lines you are not using yet.
Closed, it is a bar showing its first line. Click the bar, or the scratchpad
button in the song bar, to open it, and drag its top edge to make it taller.

Text in the scratchpad works with the writing tools like your lyrics do. Wish
Workshop and the rhyme tools can send words to it with **Add to Scratchpad**.
description: The three panels of the Lyric Genie web editor, how to resize and hide them, and what changes in a phone browser.

heading: In a phone browser
text:
Below 768 pixels wide, the workspace turns into something closer to the iOS
app.

- **The app bar goes away** while a song is open. **Songs** at the top left is
  the way back.
- **The left panel slides in over the lyrics.** The panel button at the top left
  opens it, and tapping outside closes it.
- **The right panel is a sheet from the bottom.** The tools button at the top
  right opens the writing tools. Drag the sheet's handle down, or tap above it,
  to close it.
- **The writing buttons move to a bar along the bottom:** Spark, Arrange and
  Blank, then Perform and View. While you have lyrics selected, the selection
  tools take that row instead.
- **The floating genie** in the corner opens the Genie chat. If you have turned
  it off in **Settings** (the last tab along the bottom), a Genie button appears at the top right instead.
- **The scratchpad** has no bar when closed. The scratchpad button at the top
  slides it in and out.

Narrowing a desktop window past that width folds the side panels away too.
description: The three panels of the Lyric Genie web editor, how to resize and hide them, and what changes in a phone browser.

text:
Answers here are deliberately short. Each one links to the page that goes into
it properly.
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Is there a web version
text:
Yes. The web app is at app.lyricgenie.app, and it runs in a desktop or phone
browser. Almost everything is in both apps: writing, the rhyme and syllable
tools, Wish Workshop, Genie, recordings, concepts, projects, collaboration and
Pro.

A few things are in one app only:

- **iPhone only:** Freestyle, transcribing voice memos, the share extension,
  Siri and the Action Button for recording an idea, and deleting your account.
- **Web only:** reading two tabs side by side, and, in a
  [session](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/), sharing your DAW or your screen.
  Sessions themselves are on both.

Each page of these docs says where the two differ, and the switch in the top bar
picks which one you read.
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Do my songs sync between iPhone and web
text:
Yes. Both apps use the same account, so a song written on one is there on the
other, and lyrics, recordings, concepts and projects all appear in both. Sign in
with the same Google or Apple button you use on your iPhone. See
[Signing in](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/signing-in/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Which browsers does the web app work in
text:
Recording and importing audio need Chrome, Edge or Safari, because the browser has
to be able to make AAC audio. Firefox cannot record or import audio. See
[Supported formats](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/formats/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Can I subscribe to Pro on the web
text:
Yes. Click **Upgrade** in the web app's Settings. One subscription covers the
web app and the iOS app on iPhone and iPad, so you never need two. New
subscribers get the first 14 days free, on either app. See
[Plans and Pro](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/plans/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: How do I cancel Pro
text:
Where you subscribed. If you subscribed on the web, click **Cancel
subscription** in the web app's Settings. If you subscribed in the iOS app,
cancel in your Apple ID's subscriptions, because Apple bills it. Either way you
keep Pro to the end of the period you paid for. See
[Plans and Pro](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/plans/#cancelling-do-it-where-you-subscribed).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: I have a promo code. Where does it go
text:
In the web app. Click **Upgrade** in Settings, then **Have a code?** under the
plans, and type it in. A code that makes Pro free skips the trial and does not
ask for a card. Each code works once. See [Plans and Pro](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/plans/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Does it write songs for me
text:
No, and it will not try. Every AI feature in Lyric Genie works on material you
have already given it: a line to rewrite, a song with a mood and a theme
attached, a phrase to find rhymes for. There is no button that produces a
finished song from nothing.

The closest thing is Creative Spark, which writes new material for a song that
already has an AI Context. See [Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Do I need Pro
text:
Not to write, not to record, and **not to collaborate**. The free plan gives you
unlimited songs, {{limit.recording.freeTotal}} of recordings,
{{limit.rhymes.freeDaily}} rhyme lookups a day,
{{limit.ai.freeCalls}} AI calls and {{limit.ai.freeCallsLowCost}} quick AI
calls.

Every AI feature can be tried on the free plan. Pro raises the limits, keeps
your original audio files, and lets you start [sessions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/).
See
[Plans and Pro](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/plans/) and [Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Can my collaborator use the free plan
text:
Yes. Collaboration is free on both sides. Inviting, tabs, sending lines, chat
and the Master work the same for a free collaborator as for a Pro one. That
includes [sessions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/): starting one needs Pro, but a
free collaborator can join any session a Pro writer is in.
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Do I have to sign in
text:
Yes, and it is what makes syncing work. Your songs and recordings live in your
account, so the same library appears on every device you sign in on.

Sign-in is Google or Apple. There is no email and password option. See
[Signing in](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/signing-in/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: I signed in with Google before and now I used Apple. Where are my songs
text:
In the Google account. Those are two separate accounts even with the same email
address behind them. Sign out and back in with the other button. Nothing is
lost.
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Does it work offline
text:
Writing and recording do. Transcription and every AI feature need a connection,
because the work happens on a server. If you lose the network mid-recording, the
audio is kept and the words are not.
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Can I get my lyrics out
text:
Yes, two ways. A **lyric sheet** publishes one song as a web page with your
writer credits, at a link you can send to anyone. The share action also gives
you plain text. See [Lyric sheets](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Is a lyric sheet public
text:
Anyone with the link can open it. There is no password on it and it is not
listed anywhere, so it is as private as the link is. It is also frozen at the
moment you made it.
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Can I delete a lyric sheet I already sent
text:
Yes. Open the song, choose **Lyric Sheet** from the ⋯ menu, and delete it from
the **Previous Sheets** list. The link stops working for everyone at once.

Deleting your account does not do this for you, because sheets are published
pages rather than account data. Take them down first if you want them gone. See
[Lyric sheets](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: How many people can write on one song
text:
Up to eight, you included. Invites nobody has used yet count toward the eight,
so cancel one you no longer need to make room. Each writer gets a tab. See
[Inviting a collaborator](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/#how-many-people).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Does my collaborator see me typing
text:
They can see that you are, and where. While you are both in a song, each of you
shows as here, and a collaborator who is writing shows as **Writing in** and the
section, such as Chorus. Opening a collaborator's tab also shows their cursor
and selection in their colour, and their words appear on that tab as they type
them. On the iPhone that needs version 2.22 or later.

What they cannot do is type over you. Each writer has their own tab and their
own copy of the lyrics, and you move material between them deliberately, by
sending it. The one shared tab, the Master, takes one writer at a time.

See [Collaborator tabs](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/tabs/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Can we talk while we write
text:
Yes, with a session: live video and voice with your collaborators, inside the
song, with the lyrics still in front of you. Sessions work on the web and in
the iPhone app from version 2.23, where a session behaves like a phone call.
Starting one needs Pro; joining a Pro writer's session is
free. Every shared song also has a [chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/). See
[Sessions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Can my DAW play into a session
text:
Yes, once sessions open. Put the Lyric Genie Session plugin on your DAW's
master and it sends a copy of the audio into the session, so collaborators hear
the track directly rather than through your microphone. Only the person sharing
needs it, on a Mac or PC with the web app open. Anyone can listen, including on
an iPhone. See
[Share your DAW live](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/daw-plugin/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Can I search my lyrics
text:
Yes. On the web, the search at the top of Home, or ⌘K (Ctrl K on Windows),
searches songs, every line on every tab including the Master, notes, chat,
recordings, ideas, concepts and projects. In the iOS app, the search on the
Songs tab matches titles, lyrics and AI Context. See
[Search everything](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/search/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: What is the Master tab for
text:
The version you have agreed on. Anyone on the song can type in it, one writer
at a time: whoever is typing holds a lock on the Master tab until they let go or
stop for 30 seconds. You can also send your best sections to it from your own
tab. See [The Master](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/master/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Can I import lyrics I wrote somewhere else
text:
Yes. Paste them in, or import a file. Section headers are recognised on the way
in, with or without brackets, so `[Chorus]` and `Chorus` both become a chorus.
See [Importing files](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/importing/).
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Why did my stanza spacing change
text:
It should not any more. A version before 2.18 could flatten the spacing of
earlier stanzas while you typed, and leaving the song and returning would restore
it. Update if you are seeing it.
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

heading: Something is broken
text:
Start at [Troubleshooting](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/troubleshooting/). If it is not there, email the
address at the bottom of this page with your device and app version.
description: Short answers to the questions people ask before they try the app.

text:
The first time you sign in, Lyric Genie takes you through eight short steps
before it lets you at the app. Most take a single tap, one is optional, and two
of them change how the app behaves afterwards.
description: The eight short steps Lyric Genie takes you through the first time you open it, what it does with the answers, and which ones matter later.
platformNote: On the web, a new account gets a short welcome on Home instead: your name, a photo (optional), what describes you, how much you've written, how you found Lyric Genie, and two preferences (in-line suggestions and the occasional email). The last step offers ways to start your first song (Genie guides you, or a blank page), or a link to join a collaborator's song with a code. You can skip it, and Home offers to finish setting up later. You change your name any time under Settings, Profile.

heading: The eight steps
text:
| Step | What it asks | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Your name** | What should we call you? | Becomes your [display name](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/profile/), which is what collaborators see. Up to eighteen characters. |
| **2. Photo** | Add a photo? | Optional. Upload one and crop it, use your Google photo, or skip. Collaborators see it next to your name. |
| **3. Role** | What best describes you? | Songwriter, Artist, Producer or Hobbyist. Pick as many as fit. |
| **4. Experience** | How much have you written? | From Just Starting to Professional. |
| **5. Where you found us** | How did you find us? | Skippable, and the only step that is purely for us. |
| **6. Voice** | Enable voice features | The real iOS microphone and speech permissions. |
| **7. Notifications** | Stay in the loop | The real iOS notification permission. |
| **8. In-line suggestions** | Enable In-line Suggestions | A switch, on by default. |

The Photo step is new in iOS 2.23. Earlier versions have seven steps.

heading: The two that matter later
text:
**Voice.** Microphone and speech recognition are system permissions, so this
step hands you to iOS. Decline and [Freestyle](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/freestyle/) and recording
cannot work at all. If you said no and changed your mind, it is in the iOS
Settings app under Lyric Genie, not in Lyric Genie itself.

**In-line suggestions.** The last step is the same switch that lives in
[Preferences](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/preferences/), so whatever you choose here you can change
whenever you like. See [In-line suggestions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/inline-suggestions/).

The last step offers ways to start your first song (Genie guides you, or a blank page), or a link to join a collaborator's song with a code. You can skip it, and Home offers to finish setting up later. You change your name any time under Settings, Profile.

heading: The ones that do not
text:
Your role and your experience level are saved to your profile, and that is all
they do. **They do not steer the writing tools.** A professional and a beginner
get the same suggestions from the same song.

What actually shapes what the AI writes is the song's
[AI Context](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/), which is mood, theme and similar artists, and your
[AI Style](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/ai-style/) settings. Both are per-account or per-song and
both can be changed any time.

A new account goes straight into [the song wizard](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/song-wizard/), so

Nothing here is asked again. If you want to change an answer, your name and
photo are in [your profile](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/profile/), the suggestions switch is in
[Preferences](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/preferences/), and the two permissions are in the iOS
Settings app.

text:
This is the short path through the app. Every step links to the page that covers
it properly, so read this once and then go deeper wherever you need to.
description: From an empty account to a finished draft you can sing, in ten minutes.

heading: 1. Sign in
text:
Lyric Genie signs in with Google or with Apple. There is no email and password
form. Pick one and remember which, because they are separate accounts and your
songs belong to whichever you used. See [Signing in](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/signing-in/).

Web app:
On the web, **Continue with Google** or **Continue with Apple** opens a small
sign-in window, so allow pop-ups for the site if nothing appears.
description: From an empty account to a finished draft you can sing, in ten minutes.

heading: 2. Start from the Start tab
text:
Web app:
Everything begins on **Home**, the page you land on after signing in, or the
logo in the top left from anywhere else. Its round buttons are the ways in:
**Write** opens a new song, **Record** captures an idea as audio, and **Concept**
saves an idea you are not ready to write as a [concept](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/concepts/). See
[The Home page](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/home/).

iPhone and iPad app:
Everything begins here. The four circles are the four ways in.

iPhone and iPad app:
| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Write** | Opens a new song. Choose a guided start or a blank page. |
| **Freestyle** | Starts recording straight away, and turns what you sang into lyrics. |
| **Record** | Captures audio with no song attached to it yet. |
| **Concept** | Saves an idea you are not ready to write. |

If you have nothing at all in mind, tap **Write**. If you have a melody in your
head, tap **Freestyle** and sing it. See [Freestyle](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/freestyle/).

Web app:
Freestyle is not in the web app yet, so a song starts from **Write** on Home, or
**New Song** on the [Songs](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/songs/) page.
description: From an empty account to a finished draft you can sing, in ten minutes.

heading: 3. Answer three questions
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Tapping Write offers a **Guided Start** or a **Blank Editor**. Take the guided
one the first time.

Web app:
A new song asks how you want to start: **Guide me** or **Start from scratch**.
Take the guided one the first time. Genie, the chat panel beside your lyrics,
asks the three questions one at a time. See [Guided Start](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/).

The three questions are mood, theme, and similar artists. They are worth
answering honestly, because they are not a quiz: they become the song's **AI
Context**, and every AI feature in the app reads them from then on. A song with
no context gets generic help. A song with context gets help that sounds like
your song.

The guided start then offers titles and opening phrases. Take what you like and ignore
the rest. See [The song wizard](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/song-wizard/).
description: From an empty account to a finished draft you can sing, in ten minutes.

heading: 4. Write, and let it find your structure
text:
You are now in the editor. Type lyrics.

Put a line reading `Chorus` on its own and the app turns it into a section
header. It recognises the usual names with or without brackets, so `Chorus`,
`[Chorus]` and `V1` all work. That is all structure is here: labelled blocks of
text.

See [Sections and song structure](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/sections/) and
[The song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/).
description: From an empty account to a finished draft you can sing, in ten minutes.

heading: 5. Use Wish Workshop when you are stuck
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
**Wish**, the lamp in the bar along the bottom of the editor, opens **Wish
Workshop**. It behaves two ways:

Web app:
**Wish Workshop** is the sparkle button in the song bar above your lyrics. It
behaves two ways:

- **Nothing selected.** It offers Creative Spark and writes something new for
  the song.
- **Text selected.** It rewrites that text, holding the syllable count and the
  rhyme unless you tell it not to.

That difference catches everyone once. If it rewrote a line when you wanted new
material, deselect and try again. See [Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/).

For smaller help there is a rhyme tool, a thesaurus, and a syllable adjuster,
all in the bar that appears when you select a line. See
[Selecting and editing lines](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/selecting/).

**Genie** is something else: a chat beside the song, where you can ask for
ideas in plain words, or ask how something in the app works. On iOS it is the
**Genie** button in the bottom bar; on the web, the genie in the corner of the
editor. See [Genie](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/).
description: From an empty account to a finished draft you can sing, in ten minutes.

heading: 6. Sing it
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Tap **Perform** and the song goes full screen: black background, white words,
nothing else. It is for singing from rather than writing in, and the font size
slider is there because the phone is usually on a stand.

Web app:
Click **Perform** and the song goes full screen: black background, white words,
nothing else. It is for singing from rather than writing in, and the text size
control is there because the screen is usually across the room.

See [Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/).
description: From an empty account to a finished draft you can sing, in ten minutes.

heading: 7. Get it out of the app
text:
Two things are worth knowing when you want to show someone.

- A **lyric sheet** publishes the song as a web page with your writer credits on
  it, at a link you can send to anyone. It is a frozen snapshot, so later edits
  do not change a link you already sent. See
  [Lyric sheets](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/).
- A **collaborator** can be invited to the song itself, with a six character code.
  Collaboration is free on both sides. See
  [Inviting a collaborator](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/).
description: From an empty account to a finished draft you can sing, in ten minutes.

heading: What to read next
text:
[How it fits together](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/how-it-fits-together/) is the one page that saves you
time later. It explains why a recording you made on the Start tab is not inside
the song you thought it was, which is the single most common confusion in the
app.
description: From an empty account to a finished draft you can sing, in ten minutes.

text:
The Lyric Genie Session plugin sends your DAW's output into a
[song session](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/). Your collaborators hear the track at
full quality, without the voice processing a microphone gets, and see your
DAW's tempo and position, such as **▶ 92 BPM · bar 17**.

Only the person sharing their DAW needs the plugin. Everyone else just joins the
session, on the web or on the iPhone app.
description: Stream your DAW's audio and tempo into a song session with the Lyric Genie Session plugin for Mac and Windows, so collaborators hear the track at full quality.
platformNote: The DAW plugin shares from a computer, through the web app. You can join a session on the iPhone app and hear a DAW someone else shares, but you cannot share one from the iPhone.

heading: What you need
text:
- **A Mac with macOS 11 (Big Sur) or later**, Apple silicon or Intel, or **a
  PC with 64-bit Windows 10 or later**. On a Mac the installer adds the VST3
  and AU plugins; on Windows it adds the VST3 plugin. Windows on ARM can only
  use it in a DAW running in x64 emulation. The Windows installer isn't signed
  yet, so if Windows says it protected your PC, choose **More info**, then
  **Run anyway**.
- **A DAW that loads VST3 or AU plugins.** Logic Pro, Ableton Live, Cubase, FL
  Studio, Studio One, Reaper, Bitwig and GarageBand all do, as does any other
  software that loads VST3 or AU. Pro Tools is not supported, because it only
  loads AAX plugins.
- **Lyric Genie open in Chrome or Edge**, on the same computer as the DAW. The
  plugin talks to the browser tab directly on your computer. Safari may block
  that connection.
description: Stream your DAW's audio and tempo into a song session with the Lyric Genie Session plugin for Mac and Windows, so collaborators hear the track at full quality.
platformNote: The DAW plugin shares from a computer, through the web app. You can join a session on the iPhone app and hear a DAW someone else shares, but you cannot share one from the iPhone.

heading: Installing the plugin
text:
1. Download the installer. Click **Get the plugin** in a song's Session section
   or on the session check, or **Connect** on the **Your DAW** row once you are
   in a session. Then click **Download for Mac** or **Download for Windows** in
   the **Share your DAW live** window. The installers are also at
   [app.lyricgenie.app/downloads/LyricGenieSession-0.1.1-mac.pkg](https://app.lyricgenie.app/downloads/LyricGenieSession-0.1.1-mac.pkg)
   and
   [app.lyricgenie.app/downloads/LyricGenieSession-0.1.1-windows.exe](https://app.lyricgenie.app/downloads/LyricGenieSession-0.1.1-windows.exe).
2. Open the installer and follow it.
   - **Mac:** the `.pkg` puts the VST3 and AU versions in your Mac's plug-ins
     folders, so every DAW on the Mac can find them.
   - **Windows:** the `.exe` puts the VST3 in `C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3`,
     where Windows DAWs look. If Windows says it protected your PC, choose
     **More info**, then **Run anyway**. It can be removed from **Installed apps**.
3. If your DAW was open, restart it or rescan its plug-ins so it sees
   **Lyric Genie Session**.
description: Stream your DAW's audio and tempo into a song session with the Lyric Genie Session plugin for Mac and Windows, so collaborators hear the track at full quality.
platformNote: The DAW plugin shares from a computer, through the web app. You can join a session on the iPhone app and hear a DAW someone else shares, but you cannot share one from the iPhone.

heading: Adding it to your DAW
text:
Insert **Lyric Genie Session** as an effect on your master bus. That way
collaborators hear the whole mix. You can put it on any other bus or track instead
if you only want to share that part.

The plugin does not change your own sound. Audio passes through it untouched,
and a copy goes to Lyric Genie.

### The plugin window

Open the plugin in your DAW to see what it is doing.

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Waiting for Lyric Genie** | Nothing is connected yet. Open your song in the browser and start or join its session. |
| **Connected to Lyric Genie** | The web app has found it, but is not sharing it yet. |
| **Live in** and the song's name | Collaborators hear your DAW. |
| **Can't open its connection** | The plugin could not get a connection on your computer. See [below](#if-the-plugin-cannot-open-its-connection). |

Two controls change only what the session hears:

- **The knob** sets how loud your DAW is in the session, from −24 dB to +12 dB.
  Your own output is not affected.
- **Mute send** silences the session copy while your DAW keeps playing for you.
description: Stream your DAW's audio and tempo into a song session with the Lyric Genie Session plugin for Mac and Windows, so collaborators hear the track at full quality.
platformNote: The DAW plugin shares from a computer, through the web app. You can join a session on the iPhone app and hear a DAW someone else shares, but you cannot share one from the iPhone.

heading: Connecting it to Lyric Genie
text:
The first time, tell the web app to look for the plugin:

1. With the plugin loaded in your DAW, open the **Share your DAW live** window.
   It opens from **Get the plugin** in the Session section, from **Connect** on
   the **Your DAW** row in **Audio inputs**, or from **Connect your DAW…** in
   the **Add audio input** menu.
2. Click **Check for the plugin**.
3. Chrome or Edge may ask to let Lyric Genie access other apps and services on
   this device. Allow it. That is the connection to the plugin on your own
   computer. Nothing goes over the internet until you share in a session.

If you are not in a session, the window says **Found it. It'll share when you
start a session.** If you are, it starts sharing straight away.

After that first time, this browser on this computer looks for the plugin by
itself. The session check names your DAW, for example **Steinberg Cubase is
ready. It shares when the session starts.** (or **Your DAW is ready** when the
DAW does not give its name), and once you are in, your DAW is shared without
you doing anything.
description: Stream your DAW's audio and tempo into a song session with the Lyric Genie Session plugin for Mac and Windows, so collaborators hear the track at full quality.
platformNote: The DAW plugin shares from a computer, through the web app. You can join a session on the iPhone app and hear a DAW someone else shares, but you cannot share one from the iPhone.

heading: Sharing it in a session
text:
In a session, **Your DAW** sits right under your mic in
[Audio inputs](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/#audio-inputs).

- **Shared.** The row has a meter, a volume slider for everyone, a mute button
  and an × to stop sharing. Your DAW's transport shows on the row: ▶ or ■, the
  tempo, and the bar and beat while it plays. Collaborators see the same on your
  row in their list.
- **Not shared yet.** The row says your DAW **is ready to share**. Click
  **Share**.

The plugin does not share itself when a collaborator is already sharing audio in
the session, so two tracks do not play over each other. Click **Share** on the
row when you want yours in.

If you stop sharing your DAW with the ×, it stays off until you leave and
rejoin the session, or click **Share** again.

### Duck mic

If you play your DAW through speakers rather than headphones, your mic picks
the track up too, and collaborators hear it twice. **Duck mic**, on the
**Your DAW** row, fixes that: while your DAW is playing, your mic drops by
18 dB, and it comes back as soon as you stop. Talk over a playing track and
you are quieter, so stop the track to talk.

Duck mic is on to begin with. Click it to turn it off, for example when you are
on headphones and want to sing over the track. The app remembers your choice.

While your mic is lowered, your mic row shows **Ducked**, and your collaborators
see **Ducked** on your mic in their list too, so a quieter voice is not a
mystery.

### Using it in another tab

The plugin connects to one Lyric Genie tab at a time. If another tab has it,
the row says **In use in another Lyric Genie tab** and the button reads **Use
it here**. Click it to move the plugin to this tab. The other tab shows **Your
DAW moved to another Lyric Genie tab** and does not take it back by itself.

### When sharing stops

The session shows why:

- **The plugin stopped (closed in the DAW, or the DAW quit).** Open the DAW and
  the plugin again, then click **Share**.
- **Your DAW's sample rate changed. Share the plugin again.** Changing the
  project's sample rate breaks the stream. Click **Share** to start it again at
  the new rate.
description: Stream your DAW's audio and tempo into a song session with the Lyric Genie Session plugin for Mac and Windows, so collaborators hear the track at full quality.
platformNote: The DAW plugin shares from a computer, through the web app. You can join a session on the iPhone app and hear a DAW someone else shares, but you cannot share one from the iPhone.

heading: If the plugin is not found
text:
**Check for the plugin** says **Not found** with the usual reasons:

- **The plugin is not installed.** The message links to the installer.
- **The DAW is closed, or the plugin is not loaded on a track or bus.** The
  plugin only answers while it is running inside your DAW.
- **The browser was not allowed to reach this computer.** If you said no when
  Chrome or Edge asked, click **let Lyric Genie access apps on this device** in
  the message. It copies the address of this site's settings. Paste it into
  the address bar, set **Apps on device** to **Allow**, and check again.

Lyric Genie also has to be open on the same computer as the DAW. A browser on
another machine cannot see it.

### If the plugin cannot open its connection

Each copy of the plugin needs a free connection on your computer, and there are
five. A second copy, in another track or another DAW, takes the next one. If
the plugin window says **Can't open its connection**, all five are in use.
Remove copies of the plugin you are not using. After a DAW quits, its
connection can stay taken for about a minute.
description: Stream your DAW's audio and tempo into a song session with the Lyric Genie Session plugin for Mac and Windows, so collaborators hear the track at full quality.
platformNote: The DAW plugin shares from a computer, through the web app. You can join a session on the iPhone app and hear a DAW someone else shares, but you cannot share one from the iPhone.

text:
Freestyle records you and transcribes what you sang or said into editable
lyrics. It is built for the moment where the melody arrives before the words do.
description: Sing or speak into the app and get lyrics back.
platformNote: Freestyle is not in the web app yet. The web app records audio, but it does not turn what you sing into lyrics.

heading: Starting a Freestyle
text:
There are two ways in, and they behave differently on purpose.

**From the Start tab.** Tapping Freestyle starts recording immediately. You
tapped the button because you had something to sing, and making you tap a second
time loses the take.

**From inside a song.** The microphone icon in the song editor opens Freestyle
ready but not recording. You are already in a writing session, so the app waits
for you.

If you want to set up before you sing, open a song and use the microphone icon
rather than the Start tab.
description: Sing or speak into the app and get lyrics back.
platformNote: Freestyle is not in the web app yet. The web app records audio, but it does not turn what you sing into lyrics.

heading: While you are recording
text:
The timecode counts the audio you have actually recorded. Pausing stops the
clock, and resuming picks up where it left off, so the number always matches the
length of the file rather than the time you spent with the screen open.

**Undo takes back the last segment**, meaning everything since you last started
or resumed. Sing something you would rather not keep, pause, and tap Undo, and
that stretch goes without costing you the take you already have. It is the
reason to pause between ideas rather than running one long recording.

If nothing is picked up at all, so the take is silent, it is thrown away rather
than saved as a recording of nothing.
description: Sing or speak into the app and get lyrics back.
platformNote: Freestyle is not in the web app yet. The web app records audio, but it does not turn what you sing into lyrics.

heading: When you stop
text:
Pause and the take settles into an editable page of lyrics, with the waveform
and the four buttons under it.

**The words are yours to fix.** Tap anywhere and type. Transcription hears a
mumbled line the way a stranger would, and the fastest fix is usually to correct
it now while you still remember what you sang.

**Lines you have not refined are purple.** Raw transcription is tinted, and
anything the AI has rewritten turns the normal text colour. It is a progress
bar: the purple is what has not been looked at yet.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Undo** | Steps back through the take, including an AI refine you did not like. |
| **Import** | Adds an audio file onto the end of the take. |
| **Refine** | Hands the raw transcription to the AI to tidy up. |
| **Insert** | Puts the lyrics in the song and keeps the audio. |

**Import adds to the take rather than replacing it.** The file goes on the end
as another segment, its words are transcribed and appended below the lines you
already have, and the result is still one recording. You can carry on recording
on top of it, and Undo takes the import back out again.

Tapping Import part way through a take pauses the recording first, so the file
lands after what you sang rather than behind it. If you had not sung anything
yet, that silent take is thrown away instead of being left as dead air in front
of the import.

This is not the same as [Importing files](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/importing/), which puts an
audio file into the song as a recording of its own. Here the file becomes part
of the Freestyle take you are building, so it is capped at the same length as a
take, and like Refine it needs AI access.
description: Sing or speak into the app and get lyrics back.
platformNote: Freestyle is not in the web app yet. The web app records audio, but it does not turn what you sing into lyrics.

heading: What Refine does
text:
Refine is a tidy-up, not a rewrite. It goes through the transcription and
swaps only the words that do not work, keeping the same number of lines and
the same number of syllables in each one, so the take still fits the melody you
sang it to. Placeholder sounds get the most attention: a line you filled with
*la la la* comes back as real words of the same length.

That is the whole job. Refine will not add a verse, cut a line, or reorder
anything. For writing that goes further, Insert the take and use
[Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/) on it in the editor.

### It asks for context first, every time

Tapping Refine always opens the context sheet before anything is sent, so you
can steer each run rather than being stuck with what you answered once.

These are the song's [AI Context](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/) fields, not
Freestyle-only settings. Whatever the song already has is filled in, and what
you type is what the rest of the song's AI tools will use afterwards.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Continue with Context** | Saves your answers to the song, then refines. |
| **Continue Anyway** | Refines with what is on screen without saving it. |

A specific theme is worth more than a mood. *Driving north to leave someone
behind* gives the AI something to aim at; *sad* does not.

### After it runs

The refined lines come back in the normal text colour rather than purple, and
the whole take is one step on the undo stack. If you preferred the raw version,
tap **Undo** once and it comes straight back.

Pro:
Refine is a Pro feature. The free plan includes a handful of AI calls so you
can see what it does, and Pro raises that to {{limit.ai.proMonthly}} a month.
The exact numbers are on [Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: Sing or speak into the app and get lyrics back.
platformNote: Freestyle is not in the web app yet. The web app records audio, but it does not turn what you sing into lyrics.

heading: What Insert actually does
text:
Three things at once, which is the part worth knowing.

1. **The lyrics go to the end of the song**, after a blank line if there was
   already something there. They are ordinary lines you can edit or delete.
2. **The audio is saved** as a recording on that song, called **Freestyle**.
3. **The recording is tied to the lines it produced.** Not to the song as a
   whole, to those exact words.

That third one is the reason to use Freestyle over recording and typing
separately. Months later the take is still attached to the lines that came out
of it, so you can play back how you sang them. See
[Recordings in a song](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/recordings/).

**Cancel throws the audio away.** Backing out of Freestyle deletes the recording
rather than leaving it in the Recordings tab. If a take is worth keeping, Insert
it, even if the words need work.

heading: When transcription has a problem
text:
Transcription needs a network connection. The audio does not. If transcription
fails, you get a message saying so, and the recording keeps going. Your audio is
still captured and still saved.

stops and tells you why rather than cutting out silently.

Full numbers are on [Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
