text:
Lyric Genie imports two different kinds of file: audio, which becomes a
[recording](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/), and text, which becomes lyrics.

iPhone and iPad app:
There are two routes in. Pick a file from inside the app, or send something to
Lyric Genie from another app's share sheet.

Web app:
On the web you pick a file from your computer. There is no share sheet, so the
iOS route of sending something from another app does not apply.
description: Bringing audio and lyrics in from elsewhere, by file or from the share sheet.

heading: Picking a file
text:
Web app:
Each kind has its own button. **Import Lyrics** sits beside the search field on
the **Songs** page and takes text documents. **Upload Audio** sits at the top of
the **Recordings** page and takes audio files. Both open your browser's file
picker.

iPhone and iPad app:
The import button in the top bar of the **Start**
tab takes either kind. The app works out what it got by inspecting the file
itself, not by trusting the extension, so a mislabelled file still lands in the
right place. Audio goes to Recordings. Text goes to lyrics.

iPhone and iPad app:
If you already know what you are importing, the tab menus are explicit.

| Where | Menu item | Takes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Songs tab ⋯ | **Import Lyrics from File** | Text documents |
| Recordings tab ⋯ | **Import Audio from File** | Audio files |

These two were both labelled "Import from Files" in older versions, which made
them impossible to tell apart. They now say which is which.
description: Bringing audio and lyrics in from elsewhere, by file or from the share sheet.

heading: Sharing from another app (iPhone and iPad)
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Lyric Genie appears in the iOS share sheet, which is the route most people
actually use. It works from **Voice Memos**, **Notes**, **Files**, **Mail**, and
anything else that shares audio or text.

From Voice Memos: press and hold a memo, tap **Share**, and pick Lyric Genie.
The app opens with the audio already imported and waiting in Recordings. Nothing
is exported to your camera roll or your Files app on the way.

**Audio always wins.** If what you share contains both audio and text, Lyric
Genie takes the audio and ignores the rest. Share them separately if you want
both.

**One at a time.** Only the most recent thing you shared is held. Share two
memos in quick succession, before opening the app, and the second replaces the
first.
description: Bringing audio and lyrics in from elsewhere, by file or from the share sheet.

heading: What the app does with shared text
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Sharing a note or a document opens an **Import Song** sheet rather than dropping
the text straight into a song. Nothing is created until you tap Import.

Web app:
Picking a text file opens an **Import Song** sheet rather than dropping the text
straight into a song. It shows the lyrics, the context it found and an editable
title, and lets you file the song in a project. Nothing is created until you
click Import. A file that is too large or cannot be read says so instead.

### The three magic lines

If your text contains any of these lines, the app takes them out of the lyrics
and puts them in the song's AI Context instead.

```
Mood: restless, electric
Theme: falling for someone who scrambles your signal
Similar Artists: MGMT, The 1975
```

Matching ignores capitals and spacing around the colon, and only the first of
each is used. Everything else stays as lyrics. It means a note you keep in
another app can carry its own context in, and the song arrives ready for the
writing tools.

### Where the title comes from

Web app:
The **first non-empty line** of the text, taken out of the lyrics. If the file is
empty, the file's name is used, and failing that **Imported Note**. The title
field on the sheet is editable either way.

iPhone and iPad app:
Whatever the sharing app calls it. Apple Notes sends the note's own title, so
that is what you get. If nothing sends a title, the app takes the **first
non-empty line** of the text and removes it from the lyrics. Failing both, the
song is called **Imported Note**.

The title field on the sheet is editable either way.
description: Bringing audio and lyrics in from elsewhere, by file or from the share sheet.

heading: Where imported audio lands
text:
Audio does not simply fall into the Recordings tab. The import sheet asks you
first, under an **IMPORT TO** heading.

Web app:
On the web, the sheet also shows a preview and lets you name the take. It offers
**Ideas** or any of your songs, and the same two choices below apply.

- **Ideas** leaves it unattached, filed with your other unassigned recordings.
- **Any song** attaches it straight away, so it never spends time as a loose
  idea. A search field appears once you have more than five songs, and shared
  songs are marked with a **Collaborative** badge.

The sheet also lets you name the take before it arrives, instead of leaving it
called Recording and the time of day.

Choosing the song here saves the single most common bit of confusion in the app,
which is a recording you cannot find because it is sitting unattached. See
[How it fits together](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/how-it-fits-together/).
description: Bringing audio and lyrics in from elsewhere, by file or from the share sheet.

heading: What happens to imported audio
text:
Audio is converted to M4A on your device as it comes in (in your browser, on the
web, which needs Chrome, Edge or Safari). A long WAV shrinks
considerably in the process, which is why there is no file size ceiling worth
worrying about. What matters is length, not megabytes.

Length is capped exactly the way recording is: {{limit.recording.freePerItem}}
per item on the free plan, {{limit.recording.proPerItem}} on Pro. Importing is
not a way around the recording limit.

Pro:
Pro also keeps the file you imported exactly as it was, so a WAV stays a WAV
alongside the converted take. Download it again with **Download Original** from
the take's menu. See [Original files](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/plans/#original-files).

If a file is longer than your plan allows, the import is refused and the message
tells you how long the file was. Trim it and try again.
description: Bringing audio and lyrics in from elsewhere, by file or from the share sheet.

heading: Limits on imported text
text:
A text file has to be under **5 MB**, which is far more lyrics than anyone has.
A file that cannot be read at all says so rather than importing blank.

page: Siri, the Action Button and shortcuts
text:
An idea rarely waits for you to unlock your phone and find the right screen.
Lyric Genie gives Siri, the Action Button and Control Center three things it
can do straight away: record an idea, start a new song, and start a Freestyle.

None of them needs setting up for Siri. Say the phrase and it works.
description: Record an idea in Lyric Genie without opening the app, from Siri, the Action Button, Control Center or the Lock Screen, and start a song or a Freestyle the same way.
platformNote: Siri, the Action Button and Control Center are iPhone features, so this page is for the iOS app. On the web, Record on Home or the Recordings page catches an idea the same way.

page: Siri, the Action Button and shortcuts
heading: Record an Idea
text:
**Record an Idea** starts recording the moment you ask, without opening the
app. Run it again to stop, and the take is saved to your Ideas in
[Recordings](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/), named with the date and time, such as
**Idea · Oct 15, 3:42 PM**. From there you can add it to a song or start a new
one from it.

Any of these phrases starts it:

- "Hey Siri, record an idea in Lyric Genie"
- "Hey Siri, start recording in Lyric Genie"
- "Hey Siri, new idea in Lyric Genie"

That works from the Lock Screen, and in the car through Siri.

### While it records

A Live Activity shows the timer on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island,
with a **Stop** button. Tap **Stop**, or run Record an Idea again, and the take
is saved.

A take stops by itself after 60 minutes, in case you forget it is running.

### What it needs

- **iOS 18 or later** to record in the background. On iOS 17, Record an Idea
  opens the app's recorder instead.
- **Lyric Genie 2.23 or later.**
- **The microphone allowed.** If you have never allowed it, open the app once
  and say yes when it asks. Siri tells you if this is the problem.
- **No live session running.** A [session](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/) is using
  the microphone, so Record an Idea says so and does nothing.

On an iPhone with an Action Button, one press can start an idea and the next

1. Open the **Settings** app, then **Action Button**.
2. Swipe to **Shortcut**, and tap **Choose a Shortcut**.
3. Under **Lyric Genie**, choose **Record an Idea**.

You can choose **New Song** or **Start Freestyle** there instead.

text:
Starting at a blank page is the hardest part. The song wizard asks three
questions, then generates a title and some phrases so there is something on the
page before you begin.
description: A guided way to start a song. Answer three questions and Lyric Genie hands you a title and some phrases to begin from.

heading: Getting there
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
From the **Start** tab, tap **Write** and choose **Guided Start**. The other
option, **Blank Editor**, skips all of this and opens an empty song.

Web app:
Click **New Song** on Home or the Songs page. The new song asks how you want to
start: **Guide me** runs the guided start, and **Start from scratch** skips all
of this and gives you an empty page. Closing the question is the same as
starting from scratch. The guided start runs as a conversation with Genie in the
chat panel beside your lyrics. See [Genie](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/).
description: A guided way to start a song. Answer three questions and Lyric Genie hands you a title and some phrases to begin from.

heading: The three questions
text:
They are the same three fields as the AI Context bar in
[the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/), asked one at a time. Whatever you answer is saved
to the song, so filling them in here means not doing it later.

Each step offers suggestion chips, and **More** reshuffles them if none fit.
**Skip** moves past any question you would rather not answer.

Web app:
On the web Genie asks each question in the chat. Click a chip or type your own
answer, use **More ideas** if none fit, and **Skip** to pass. If some of the
context is already filled in, Genie only asks the missing questions.

| Step | What it is asking | How many |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **What's the mood?** | How the song should feel. | Up to three. |
| **What's the theme?** | What happens in it, in a sentence. | One. |
| **Similar Artists** | Who inspires the sound. | Up to two. |

Theme earns the most. "The more specific, the better the suggestions" is the
app's own advice, and it is right. A sentence beats a word.
description: A guided way to start a song. Answer three questions and Lyric Genie hands you a title and some phrases to begin from.

heading: Then it sparks
text:
With your three answers in hand, the wizard generates ideas from them. This step
is called **Spark**, and it comes in two parts.

### Titles

Eight at a time. **Brainstorm More Titles** replaces them with a new set from
the same brief, so you can keep going until something lands. You do not have to
take one.

Web app:
On the web Genie lists the titles in the chat. **Brainstorm more titles** adds
another batch, and **Skip titles** moves on. Picking one sets it as the song's
title and, if the lyrics are empty, drops a section skeleton in.

### Phrases

These are fragments rather than finished lyrics: *lost the plot again*,
*wearing someone else's face*, *ghost of my own making*. Tick the ones worth
keeping and **Add to Lyrics** drops them into the song.

Web app:
On the web the lines that go with your chosen title appear as chips. Click one to
add it to the lyrics under Verse 1, click **Done** when you have enough, or
**Skip lines**.

Take more than you need. A phrase you do not use costs nothing to delete, and
the one that unlocks the song is rarely the one you expected.

**Skip Spark** leaves at any point, and you still get a song with your mood,
theme and artists filled in.
description: A guided way to start a song. Answer three questions and Lyric Genie hands you a title and some phrases to begin from.

heading: The same idea, elsewhere
text:
Spark is not only in the wizard. Open
[Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/) without selecting any text and you get
**Creative Spark**, which does the same job for a song already under way.

iPhone and iPad app:
There is also a tool that runs the other way round. **Refine Context**, the
sparkle button on the AI Context bar, takes a rough idea in plain English and
generates the mood, theme and artists from it. Spark turns a brief into ideas.
Refine Context turns a feeling into the brief.

Two switches on that sheet decide how much of the song it is allowed to build
on. **Consider Existing Title** lets it read the title you already have, and
**Consider Existing Context Fields** lets it read whatever is already in the
three fields. Leave both on to refine what you have. Turn both off to start
over from the description alone.

Web app:
There is also a tool that runs the other way round. **Refine**, beside the
**AI Context** heading in the song's side panel, offers options for the mood,
theme and artists, built from what the song already has. It says **Suggest**
while the fields are still empty. Spark turns a brief into ideas. Refine turns
a feeling into the brief.

Each field can be kept as it is or left open to change. Type what the song is
about, or what you want to change, then apply a whole option, or click single
fields to take only those. **Talk it through with Genie** moves the
conversation to [Genie](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/) instead.

iPhone and iPad app:
Refine Context then offers you a set of concepts to choose between rather than
overwriting anything. Pick one and tap **Apply**, or **New Search** to ask
again.

Pro:
Spark and Refine Context both need AI access, so they are Pro features. See
[Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: A guided way to start a song. Answer three questions and Lyric Genie hands you a title and some phrases to begin from.

heading: What you end up with
text:
A song in the editor with a title, your three context fields, and any phrases
you picked already in the lyrics. Nothing is locked in. The title can be
changed, the phrases are ordinary lines you can delete.

If you skipped the title step, the song is called **My Song** until you rename
it.
description: A guided way to start a song. Answer three questions and Lyric Genie hands you a title and some phrases to begin from.

text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Lyric Genie has five tabs. Four of them hold a different kind of object, and the
fifth is Settings.

Web app:
The web app has five places, which work the same way as the iOS tabs: **Home**,
**Songs**, **Concepts**, **Recordings** and **Settings**. On a desktop, Songs,
Concepts and Recordings run across the top bar, Home is the logo on the left, and
Settings is in the menu under your avatar in the top right. In a narrow browser
window all five become a bar along the bottom, as on iPhone. Four of them hold a
different kind of object, and Settings is the fifth. The magnifying glass in
the top bar, or `⌘` `K`, searches all of them at once. See
[Search everything](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/search/).

Each one has a page of its own. Start with whichever tab you are standing in.

iPhone and iPad app:
| Tab | Holds | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [**Start**](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/start/) | nothing of its own | The launch pad. Jump straight into writing or recording. |
| [**Songs**](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/songs/) | Songs | The documents you write lyrics in. |
| [**Concepts**](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/concepts/) | Concepts | Ideas you have not turned into songs yet. |
| [**Recordings**](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/recordings/) | Recordings | Every piece of audio you have captured, in one list. |
| [**Settings**](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/settings/) | — | Account, plan, preferences. |

Web app:
| Page | Holds | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [**Home**](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/home/) | nothing of its own | Where you pick up your last song, search everything, or start something new. |
| [**Songs**](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/songs/) | Songs | The documents you write lyrics in. |
| [**Concepts**](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/concepts/) | Concepts | Ideas you have not turned into songs yet. |
| [**Recordings**](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/recordings/) | Recordings | Every piece of audio you have captured, in one list. |
| [**Settings**](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/settings/) | — | Account, appearance, writing preferences. Opened from your avatar on desktop. |

The rest of this page is the part the tab pages do not cover: how the things in
them relate to each other.
description: Five tabs, four kinds of object, and the relationships between them.

heading: The one relationship that matters
text:
A **Recording belongs to a Song.** Not to the Recordings tab.

The Recordings tab is a view across all your audio, the way a photo library is a
view across photos that also live in albums. When you record from inside a song,
the audio is attached to that song and also appears in the Recordings list. When
you record from the Start tab, there is no song yet, so the audio lands in the
Recordings list unattached until you assign it.

This is why the Recordings tab has an **Add to Song** action and the song editor
does not. From the song's side, the recording is already there.

That single fact explains most of the "where did my recording go" confusion. If
you recorded something and cannot find it in a song, it is almost certainly
sitting unattached in Recordings, waiting to be assigned.
description: Five tabs, four kinds of object, and the relationships between them.

heading: The rest of the shape
text:
**Concepts** sit upstream of songs. A concept is a title, a mood, a theme, and
optionally some similar artists. It is the note you make when you have the idea
but not the song. When you are ready, a concept becomes a song.

**Projects** sit above songs. A project is a named, colour-tagged folder that
holds a list of songs. An album, an artist you write for, a session. A song can
be in several projects at once, or in none.

**Collaborators** sit inside a song. Each collaborator gets their own tab and their
own colour, so you can see who wrote what, and there is a Master tab where the
agreed version gets assembled.

So, reading from smallest to largest:

```
Concept ──becomes──▶ Song ──grouped into──▶ Project
                      │
                      ├── Lyrics (yours, plus a tab per collaborator, plus Master)
                      └── Recordings ──also listed in──▶ the Recordings tab
```
description: Five tabs, four kinds of object, and the relationships between them.

heading: Where your work is stored
text:
Everything syncs to your account, so the same songs and recordings appear on any
device you sign in on. Signing in is what makes that work. If you are not signed
in, you are not syncing.

Web app:
That includes the iOS app. Sign in to the web app with the same Google or Apple
account you use on your iPhone and you see the same songs, concepts, projects and
recordings, and a change made in one shows up in the other.

Open a song on a desktop browser and the editor becomes a workspace with panels
on either side of your lyrics. See [The desktop workspace](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/workspace/).
description: Five tabs, four kinds of object, and the relationships between them.

text:
Lyric Genie Docs

What everything in the app is, where it lives, and how the pieces connect.

Lyric Genie is a songwriter's notepad. You write lyrics, you capture ideas by voice, and the app keeps the two attached to each other so a hummed melody and the verse it belongs to never drift apart. Lyric Genie comes in two apps that share one account: the iOS app on iPhone and iPad, and the web app at app.lyricgenie.app. Use the **iOS / Web** switch in the top bar to pick yours. Where the two differ, the page says so, and the rest is the same for both. These docs are organised the way the app is: a page for each tab, a page for each kind of thing you make, and a page for every tool in the editor. Almost every question about Lyric Genie turns out to be a question about which thing something belongs to, which is why [How it fits together](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/how-it-fits-together/) is short and worth reading once.

heading: Where to start
text:
If you are new, [Your first song](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/first-song/) walks the whole app in ten
minutes. Then read [How it fits together](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/how-it-fits-together/), which covers
the one thing that trips most people up: a recording is not stored inside the tab
you made it in.

If you just want a quick answer, try the [FAQ](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/faq/). If a word in the app means
something you cannot guess, it is in the [Glossary](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/glossary/). If
something is not behaving, go to [Troubleshooting](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/troubleshooting/).

If you want to know exactly how long a recording can be or how many lookups you
get on the free plan, that is on [Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/), which is
generated from the app's own configuration rather than typed by hand.
description: What everything in the app is, where it lives, and how the pieces connect.

heading: A note on these docs
text:
Screenshots here are taken from the current release. A screenshot labelled
*iOS app screen* has no web version yet, and the web app's own screens are
captioned as such. Where a screenshot has a red
ring on it, the ring is pointing at the thing the surrounding paragraph is
talking about.

Anything missing, wrong, or confusing is worth an email. The address is at the
bottom of every page.
description: What everything in the app is, where it lives, and how the pieces connect.

text:
A concept is a song idea before it is a song. It holds a title, a mood, a theme
and some similar artists. It does not hold lyrics, because an idea with lyrics
is a song.

The app's own description is the clearest one: concepts are creative starting
points that shape a song before you write a single word.

Concepts live in their own tab so a half-formed idea does not clutter your list
of real work in progress.

They are laid out as a grid of cards. See
[The Concepts tab](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/concepts/).
description: Ideas you have not turned into songs yet, and the one AI feature that makes them for you.

heading: Writing one
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Tap **+** on the Concepts tab and a blank card appears in place, with the four
fields on it.

Web app:
Click **New Concept** on the Concepts page, or the empty **Click to Add** card
at the end of the grid, and a blank card opens in place with the four fields
on it. **Cancel** drops it and **Done** keeps it.

Only the title is required. Whatever you fill in carries across when the concept
becomes a song, and lands in that song's AI Context.
description: Ideas you have not turned into songs yet, and the one AI feature that makes them for you.

heading: Letting the app write them
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
The sparkle button in the top right generates concepts from what you have
already written.

Web app:
The **Generate** button in the page header generates concepts from what you have
already written.

iPhone and iPad app:
**Learn what I like from my existing songs** is on by default, and it is what
makes the results sound like you rather than like nobody. Turn it off and you
get generic ideas.

Web app:
The web dialog has two switches under **Learn what I like from**: **My songs**,
which is on by default once you have at least three songs, and **My concepts**,
which keeps it from handing you an idea you already have. **My songs** is what
makes the results sound like you rather than like nobody. Turn it off and you
get generic ideas. A stepper sets how many to generate, four to start with.
description: Ideas you have not turned into songs yet, and the one AI feature that makes them for you.

heading: Reading and using one
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Tap a card and it expands to show the whole thing, with the actions underneath.

Web app:
Click a card and it expands to show the whole thing, with the actions underneath:
**New Song**, the colour circle, **3 Similar**, and a ⋯ menu with **Edit**,
**Duplicate** and **Delete**. Clicking an open card again also edits it.

**New Song** is the point of the whole tab. The new song opens with its AI
Context already filled in, so the writing tools have something to work with from
the first line you type.

The circle beside it is the card's colour. You do not have to set one: every
new concept takes the next colour along from the last one you made, and a
generated batch walks the same seven, so a full tab reads as a grid of colours
without anyone choosing them. Tap the circle to step that card on to the next
colour yourself (click it, on the web). It is purely visual — nothing sorts or filters by it.
description: Ideas you have not turned into songs yet, and the one AI feature that makes them for you.

heading: Where else concepts come from
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Press and hold any song in the Songs tab and you get two more routes.

Web app:
Open the ⋯ menu on any song in the Songs page and you get two more routes.

- **Add to Concepts** turns that song back into an idea. Useful when a song
  turns out to be something you are not ready for.
- **Generate 3 Similar Concepts** reads the song in front of you and proposes
  three adjacent ideas.

Web app:
Both appear on a concept's own card too, as **3 Similar** for that concept. You
can also drag cards to put them in the order you want.
description: Ideas you have not turned into songs yet, and the one AI feature that makes them for you.

heading: Deleting one
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
The **X** on a card asks before it deletes, and the deletion is permanent. There
is no archive for concepts the way there is for songs.

Web app:
**Delete** in a card's ⋯ menu asks before it deletes, and the deletion is
permanent. There is no archive for concepts the way there is for songs.
description: Ideas you have not turned into songs yet, and the one AI feature that makes them for you.

text:
A project is a named folder of songs. An album, an artist you write for, a
single writing session, a batch you are pitching.

A project holds songs and nothing else. No lyrics of its own, no recordings, no
concepts. Every song in a project is also in All Songs, because a project is a
view of your songs rather than a place they move to.
description: Folders you make yourself, to group songs into an album, a client, or a session.

heading: Making one
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Open the **Songs** tab and tap **New Project** under the Projects heading, or
the folder button in the top right. It asks for a name and a colour.

Web app:
Open the **Songs** page and click the **+** beside **Projects** in the Library
panel, or **New Project** if you have none yet. It asks for a name and a colour.

The colour is the same set of seven that concepts use, and it is offered
already picked: each new project is suggested the colour after the last one you
made, so a row of projects varies without you choosing. Tap a different swatch
if you have one in mind. There is no description field, so the name is still
doing most of the work. "Winter EP" beats "New Project 2".
description: Folders you make yourself, to group songs into an album, a client, or a session.

heading: What the colour does
text:
It shows in three places.

- **The folder icon** in the Collections list takes the colour, so you can pick
  a project out of a list of them without reading.
- **The heading** when you open the project, with the same coloured folder to
  the left of the name.
- **A line above the song title**, naming every project the song is filed in,
  each in its own colour. A song in two projects names both. A song in none has
  no line.

That line looks the same wherever you see the song. Inside a project, that
project is listed first rather than left out, so a row reads the same here as
it does in All Songs and you can always see at a glance which other folders a
song is in.

**Tap a folder name to go to that folder** (click it, on the web). The rest of
the row still opens the song, and so does the name of the folder you are already
inside — there is nowhere for that one to take you.

The name is there rather than a bare coloured dot on purpose. In Lyric Genie a
coloured dot already means a person: on the collaborator tabs, beside a name on
the Collaborators screen, and in the green "who is in this song now" badge at
the right of a song row. A folder with a name on it cannot be misread as any of
those.
description: Folders you make yourself, to group songs into an album, a client, or a session.

heading: Putting songs in it
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Open the project and tap **Add Songs**, or the **+** in its top right. You get
your whole library with a checkbox on each row and a search field at the bottom.

Web app:
Open the project and click **Add Songs** in the row of buttons above the list.
You get your whole library with a checkbox on each row and a search field.

iPhone and iPad app:
You can also start from the song: press and hold it anywhere in the Songs tab
and choose **Add to Project**.

Web app:
On the web, open the song's ⋯ menu in the song list and choose **Add to
Project**.

A song can be in as many projects as you like, or in none. The same song can
sit in an album folder and a pitching folder at once, because a project is a
view of your songs rather than a place they move to.
description: Folders you make yourself, to group songs into an album, a client, or a session.

heading: Taking a song out
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Swipe the song sideways inside the project.

Web app:
Inside the project, point at the song and a **Remove** button appears at the
right of its row.

**Remove** takes the song out of the project. The song itself is untouched and
still in All Songs. Nothing in a project is ever the only copy of anything.
description: Folders you make yourself, to group songs into an album, a client, or a session.

heading: Renaming, duplicating and deleting
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Press and hold a project on the Songs tab.

Web app:
Open the project. **Edit**, **Duplicate** and **Delete** are in the row of
buttons above its songs.

**Edit** opens the same sheet as creating one, with the name and colour filled
in. **Duplicate** makes a second folder holding the same songs. **Delete** removes
the folder and leaves every song in it alone, which is the one thing worth being
sure of before you tap it.
description: Folders you make yourself, to group songs into an album, a client, or a session.

text:
A recording is a piece of audio. You make one by recording in the app, or by
importing a file you already have.

Every recording either belongs to a song or does not yet. Both kinds appear in
the **Recordings** tab, which is a list of all your audio regardless of where it
came from.

See [The Recordings tab](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/recordings/) for that list and its controls.
description: Audio, where it lives, and how it attaches to a song.

heading: The two ways audio gets created
text:
**Recorded inside a song.** Open a song, record, and the audio is attached to
that song from the moment you stop. It also shows up in the Recordings tab.

iPhone and iPad app:
**Recorded or imported on its own.** Record from the Start tab, import a file
into the Recordings tab, or say "Hey Siri, record an idea in Lyric Genie", and
there is no song to attach it to yet. It sits in Recordings unattached, as an
idea. See [Siri and the Action Button](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/siri-shortcuts/).

Web app:
**Recorded or imported on its own.** Click **Record** or **Upload Audio** at the
top of the Recordings page, and there is no song to attach it to yet. It is
saved as an unattached recording, which the web app calls an Idea. A record bar
docks at the bottom of the page while you record.

Web app:
Recording on the web needs Chrome, Edge or Safari. Firefox cannot record or
import audio, because it cannot make the AAC audio Lyric Genie stores. See
[Supported formats](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/formats/).

Unattached is a normal state, not an error. Plenty of ideas arrive before the
song they belong to exists.
description: Audio, where it lives, and how it attaches to a song.

heading: Telling the two apart
text:
The label on a row is the fastest way to know which kind you are looking at.

An unattached recording says **Song Idea** and offers **New Song** and **Add to
Song**. Once it belongs to a song, the label becomes the song's name and both
buttons disappear, because there is nothing left to decide.
description: Audio, where it lives, and how it attaches to a song.

heading: Attaching one to a song
text: **Add to Song** opens a picker of everything you have written.
description: Audio, where it lives, and how it attaches to a song.

heading: What you can do to a recording
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Tap a recording to expand it, and a ⋯ button appears with everything you can do
to it. The pencil beside the title renames it.

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Export** | Sends the audio out of the app, through the iOS share sheet. This is the only way to get a take onto your computer. |
| **Unlink from Lyrics** | Breaks the tie between a take and the specific lines it was anchored to. Only appears when there is a link to break. |
| **Download Original** | Pro. Saves the file you imported, exactly as it was. Only appears when one was kept. See [Original files](#original-files). |
| **Archive** | Takes it out of the list without deleting it. Becomes **Unarchive** afterwards. |
| **Delete** | Permanent, and it asks first. |

Archived recordings live in their own list, the same way archived songs do. An
empty one says **No Archived Recordings**.

Web app:
On the Recordings page every row's ⋯ menu holds its actions, for a take on a
song as well as a loose one.

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Open Song** | Opens the song the take belongs to. |
| **New Song from Idea** | Loose takes only. Starts a song named after it, with the take attached. |
| **Add to Song** | Loose takes only. Moves it onto a song you pick. |
| **Rename** | Edits the title in place. Clicking the name does the same. |
| **Download** | Saves the audio to your computer as an M4A file. |
| **Download Original** | Pro. Saves the file you uploaded, exactly as it was, such as a WAV. Only appears when one was kept. See [Original files](#original-files). |
| **Archive** | Takes it out of the list without deleting it. Becomes **Unarchive** afterwards. |
| **Delete** | Permanent, and it asks first. |

On a shared song you can rename, archive and delete only your own takes. The
**Archive** button at the top of the page switches to the archived list and
stays highlighted until you switch back. Inside a song, the Recordings section
also links a take to the lines it belongs to, with **Link to Lyrics** and
**Unlink from Lyrics** in its ⋯ menu, and on a shared song **Send to Chat**
shares it in the [collaborator chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/). To do the same to many takes at once, use
**Select** on the Recordings page (see [The Recordings tab](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/recordings/)).

**You can only delete your own recordings.** On a shared song you can play and
export a collaborator's take, but the Delete confirmation tells you no when it is
not yours. Nobody can quietly remove someone else's work.
description: Audio, where it lives, and how it attaches to a song.

heading: Transcription
text:
Recordings can be transcribed to text. That is what
[Freestyle](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/freestyle/) is built around: you sing or speak, and the
words come back as lyrics you can edit.

Web app:
The web app does not transcribe yet. It shows the transcript of a recording that
was transcribed on iOS, and lets you **Copy** it or **Insert into Lyrics**.

Transcription needs a network connection and recording does not, so a network
problem costs you the words and not the audio. A recording made with nothing to
hear says **Transcription unavailable**, which is honest rather than broken.
description: Audio, where it lives, and how it attaches to a song.

heading: What gets stored
text:
Audio is stored as M4A. Files you import in other formats are converted to M4A
during import, which is why a large WAV becomes a much smaller file once it is
in the app. The conversion happens on your device.

Web app:
On the web it happens in your browser, and recordings you make there are saved
as M4A too, so they play on your iPhone.

Recording length is capped per recording, and total storage is capped per
account. The free plan holds {{limit.recording.freeTotal}} in total with each
take capped at {{limit.recording.freePerItem}}. Current numbers for both plans
are on [Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).

Deleting recordings you no longer need frees the space back up.

Web app:
The web app stops a take at the per-recording cap and says so, but it does not
show the iOS low-storage alerts. **Usage & Stats** in Settings shows how much you have
used.
description: Audio, where it lives, and how it attaches to a song.

heading: Original files
text:
When you import an audio file, Lyric Genie converts it to M4A so it plays
everywhere. On Pro, the file you imported is also kept exactly as it was, so a
WAV or AIFF bounce of your demo is still there at full quality when you need it.

- **Up to 250 MB a file.** A bigger file still imports as usual, but the original
  isn't kept.
- **10 GB in total.** Once you reach it, new imports aren't kept until you delete
  some originals.
- **Collaborators can download them too.** On a shared song, everyone on it can
  save the original of any take that has one, so a collaborator gets your full-quality
  WAV without you sending it. In the web app that's **Download Original** on the
  take; the iPhone app shows it on your own takes only, for now.

The import screen tells you whether the original is being kept. Audio you send
in the [collaborator chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/) is kept the same way.

To get one back, choose **Download Original** in the take's ⋯ menu. It names
the file type, such as **Download Original (WAV)**.

iPhone and iPad app:
**Settings**, then **Original Files** under **Library**, lists every original
with its size and date, and how much of the 10 GB you are using. Tap the
download button on one to save or share it, or swipe left to delete it.

Web app:
**Original Files** in Settings opens a page listing every original with its
size, how much of the 10 GB you are using, and a search box and sort. Download
or delete them one at a time, or use **Select** to delete several.

Deleting an original never deletes the recording. The playable copy stays.

Your originals are kept for 30 days after your Pro ends. Settings shows the date
they will be deleted, and you get an email. Download any you want to keep before
then, or renew Pro to keep them all. Your recordings themselves are not
affected.

Original files need iOS 2.22 or later. Files you imported with an older
version were not kept.
description: Audio, where it lives, and how it attaches to a song.

text:
A song is the main document in Lyric Genie. It holds your lyrics, the context
the writing tools read, any audio you attach, and, once it is shared, a tab for
every writer on it.
description: The document you write in, what you can do to one from the list, and what happens to a song you are finished with.

heading: What a song holds
text:
| Part | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Title** | Names the song everywhere it is listed. The editor can suggest one from your lyrics. |
| **Lyrics** | The main text, divided into [sections](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/sections/) by their headers. |
| **AI Context** | Mood, theme and similar artists. Every AI feature reads these. |
| **Scratchpad** | A private notepad that saves with the song but is not part of the lyrics. |
| **Recordings** | Audio attached to this song. See [Recordings](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/). |
| **Collaborator tabs** | One per writer on a shared song, plus Master. |

AI Context is the part people skip and then wonder why the suggestions are
bland. It is three short fields, it takes a minute, and it changes the output of
every AI feature in the app. The [song wizard](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/song-wizard/) collects it
by asking three questions.
description: The document you write in, what you can do to one from the list, and what happens to a song you are finished with.

heading: Finding one
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
The tab opens on **All Songs**, and the back arrow beside that title leads to the
collections your songs are filed in. Both are covered on
[The Songs tab](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/songs/).

Web app:
The page opens on **All Songs**, and the Library panel beside it lists the
collections your songs are filed in. A search field above the list finds songs by
title, lyrics, mood, theme, artist or collaborator. Both are covered on
[The Songs tab](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/songs/).

To find a song from anywhere, press `⌘` `K` (`Ctrl` `K` on Windows) and type a
word from its title or a line in it. See [Search everything](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/search/).
description: The document you write in, what you can do to one from the list, and what happens to a song you are finished with.

heading: Sorting and selecting
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Inside a list, the ⋯ button sorts it and turns on multi-select.

Web app:
Inside a list, the sort menu above it picks Date Created, Last Edited or Title,
ascending or descending. **Select** beside it picks several songs at once. See
[The Songs tab](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/songs/).

iPhone and iPad app:
**Import Lyrics from File** lives here rather than on the Start tab, which is
where people look for it. See [Importing files](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/importing/).

Web app:
**Import Lyrics** is the button beside the search field. See
[Importing files](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/importing/).
description: The document you write in, what you can do to one from the list, and what happens to a song you are finished with.

heading: What you can do to a song
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Press and hold any song in a list and the app shows you the lyrics, who is on
it, and the things you can do.

Web app:
The ⋯ at the right of any song in a list holds the things you can do: **Add to
Project**, **Add to Concepts**, **Generate 3 Similar Concepts**, **Duplicate as a
new song**, **Archive** and, for a song that is only yours, **Delete**. There is
no preview on the web.

**Add to Concepts** turns the song back into an idea. **Generate 3 Similar
Concepts** reads it and proposes three adjacent ones. Both are covered on
[Concepts](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/concepts/).

iPhone and iPad app:
Swiping a song sideways gets to the same two destructive actions faster.
description: The document you write in, what you can do to one from the list, and what happens to a song you are finished with.

heading: Duplicating a song (web)
text:
Web app:
**Duplicate as a new song** makes a copy you can rewrite freely, and opens it.
It is in the ⋯ menu of a song in the Songs list, and in the song editor's own
⋯ menu. To copy several at once, use **Select** on the Songs page and click
**Duplicate**.

The copy is a solo song of yours, titled with **(Copy)** after the name. It
takes:

- your lyrics (on a shared song, your own tab),
- the AI Context,
- your scratchpad.

It does not copy your collaborators' tabs, the Master or any recordings.
description: The document you write in, what you can do to one from the list, and what happens to a song you are finished with.

heading: Archive, not delete
text:
**Archive** takes a song out of All Songs without destroying anything. An
**Archive** row then appears at the bottom of the collections screen, and the
song is in it, with its lyrics, its recordings and its collaborators intact.

The songs inside keep everything.

iPhone and iPad app:
Swiping one sideways offers the way back.

Web app:
On the web, the Archive collection is called **Archived**, and **Unarchive** is
in each song's ⋯ menu.

**Delete** is permanent, and it takes the song's attached recordings with it.

Web app:
On the web, Delete is only offered for a song that is yours alone. A shared song
can be archived but not deleted from the web app. A shared song of yours that
nobody has joined yet offers **Stop Sharing & Delete** instead. See
[Inviting a collaborator](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/#deleting-a-shared-song).

If you are not sure, archive. The only thing you lose is the song's place in the
main list, and unarchiving is one swipe (one menu choice, on the web).
description: The document you write in, what you can do to one from the list, and what happens to a song you are finished with.

heading: Selecting several at once (iPhone and iPad)
text:
**Select Songs** in the ⋯ menu puts a checkbox on every row and a bar along the
bottom.
description: The document you write in, what you can do to one from the list, and what happens to a song you are finished with.

heading: Making a song
text:
Four ways, and they all end in the same editor.

| From | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| **Write** on the Start tab (iPhone and iPad) | A guided start or a blank page. See [The song wizard](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/song-wizard/). |
| **Write** on Home, or **New Song** on Songs (web) | A guided start or a blank page. See [The song wizard](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/song-wizard/). |
| **Freestyle** (iPhone and iPad) | Sing or speak first, lyrics after. See [Freestyle](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/freestyle/). |
| A **concept** | The concept's title, mood, theme and artists carried across. |
| An unattached **recording** | A new song with that audio already on it. |

Whichever you use, the song appears in All Songs and in **Latest Songs** on the
Start tab on iOS, or on Home on the web.
description: The document you write in, what you can do to one from the list, and what happens to a song you are finished with.

heading: Writing on two devices at once (web)
text:
Web app:
You can have the same song open in two places, say the web app on your computer
and a second browser window, and write in both. Each save checks what is already
saved. Lines you changed in one place and lines you changed in the other are
combined, so neither set of edits is lost.

If both places changed the same line in different ways, Lyric Genie can't know
which you meant. It keeps the version that was saved first, and saves your other
edits as a new song with **(Conflict copy)** in its title. A banner in the song
says so and links to the copy, so you can take what you need from it.
description: The document you write in, what you can do to one from the list, and what happens to a song you are finished with.

heading: Audio
text:
| Format | Extension |
| --- | --- |
| Apple audio | `.m4a`, `.caf` |
| MP3 | `.mp3` |
| WAV | `.wav` |
| AIFF | `.aiff`, `.aif` |
| AAC | `.aac`, `.mp4` |
| FLAC | `.flac` |

Everything is converted to M4A once it is in the app, on your device rather than
on a server.

Web app:
On the web the conversion happens in your browser, and the file picker offers the
same extensions. What actually opens depends on what your browser can decode, so
MP3, WAV and M4A are the safe choices. After conversion a file must be under
60 MB, which a recording within your plan's length always is.

Importing needs Chrome, Edge or Safari. Firefox cannot, because it cannot make the
AAC audio that Lyric Genie stores.

A stereo file, such as a demo, stays stereo when you import it on the web, and
is saved at a higher quality than a recording made in the browser.

Web app:
**Recording on the web.** A recording made in the browser is saved as an AAC `.m4a` (mono, 44.1 kHz), so it
plays on your iPhone as well. Recording needs a browser that can encode AAC:
Chrome, Edge or Safari. Firefox shows a message instead of recording.

Detection is based on the file's actual type rather than its name, so a file
with a misleading extension is still routed correctly.

Pro:
On Pro, the file you import is also kept exactly as it was, up to 250 MB a file
and 10 GB in all, so you can download the WAV or AIFF again later. See
[Original files](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/#original-files).
description: File types Lyric Genie can import.

heading: Photos in the chat
text:
The [collaborator chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/) takes any picture your device or
browser can open, such as a JPEG or PNG. Photos are scaled down to at most
2048 pixels on the longest side and saved as JPEG. On the web a photo can be up
to 30 MB before it is scaled.

Audio files sent in the chat take the same formats as an import, above.
description: File types Lyric Genie can import.

heading: Lyrics and text
text:
| Format | Extension |
| --- | --- |
| Plain text | `.txt` |

text:
Lyric Genie names a few things in ways that are not obvious from the outside.
This is what each one means.
description: Every word the app uses for something of its own, in one place.

heading: What you make
text:
**Song**
The document you write lyrics in. It holds the lyrics themselves, a title, an AI
Context, a Scratchpad, any recordings you attach, and on a shared song a tab per
writer. See [Songs](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/songs/).

**Concept**
An idea that is not a song yet: a title, a mood, a theme, and optionally some
similar artists. Concepts sit upstream of songs and can become one when you are
ready. See [Concepts](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/concepts/).

**Recording**
A piece of audio. A recording belongs to a song, or to nothing yet. Either way
it appears in the Recordings tab. See [Recordings](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/).

**Idea** (web)
The web app's word for a recording that belongs to no song yet, which iOS labels
**Song Idea**.

**Project**
A named, colour-tagged folder that holds a list of songs. The colour shows on
the folder and above the title of every song in it. An album, an artist
you write for, a session. See [Projects](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/projects/).
description: Every word the app uses for something of its own, in one place.

heading: Inside a song
text:
**AI Context**
Three fields attached to the song: mood, theme, and similar artists. Everything
the AI writes for that song is steered by them. The song wizard collects them by
asking you three questions. See [The song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/).

**Scratchpad**
A ruled notepad that slides up from the bottom of the editor. It saves with the
song but is not part of your lyrics, so nothing in it reaches Perform or a lyric
sheet. On a shared song each writer has their own, marked **Private · only you
can see this** with an eye icon.

**Section**
A labelled block of a song: Verse, Chorus, Bridge and so on. A line becomes a
section header when the app recognises its text, which it does with or without
brackets. See [Sections and song structure](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/sections/).

**Arrange mode**
The mode where you select whole sections by their headers and move, copy, delete
or send them, to the Master or to a collaborator. See
[Arrange mode](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/arrange-mode/).

**Perform**
Full-screen playback of the lyrics: black background, white words, no controls
in the way. For singing from, not writing in. See [Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/).

**Lyric sheet**
A published web page of one song's lyrics, with writer credits, at its own link.
It is a **frozen snapshot**, so editing the song afterwards does not change a
link you already sent. See [Lyric sheets](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/).
description: Every word the app uses for something of its own, in one place.

heading: The AI features
text:
**Wish Workshop**
The genie lamp. With text selected it rewrites that text; with nothing selected
it offers Creative Spark. Its requests are called **wishes**, and the row of
chips above the field are ready-made ones. See
[Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/).

**Genie** (web)
The chat panel beside your lyrics in the web app, where you ask for ideas in
plain words and where Guided Start runs. See [Genie](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/).

**Creative Spark**
What Wish Workshop does when nothing is selected: writes new material for the
song rather than reworking a line you already have.

**Refine Context**
Reads your song and suggests AI Context fields for you, instead of you filling
them in by hand. It uses your AI calls.

**AI Style**
Standing instructions that apply to every AI call in every song: a paragraph of
style guidance, and a list of words you never want the AI to use. See
[AI Style](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/ai-style/).

**In-line suggestions**
Ghost text that appears ahead of your cursor when you pause while writing. Tab
or tap to accept. Silent if you do not have AI access. See
[In-line suggestions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/inline-suggestions/).

**Anchor**
In the rhyme tool, one of the two stressed syllables the app picks out of your
phrase. Rhymes are offered for each anchor separately, and for both at once. See
[Rhymes](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/rhymes/).

**Faithfulness score**
The colour-coded number on a syllable-adjusted line, saying how close the new
line stayed to your meaning. The highest score is not always the best line. See
[Syllables](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/syllables/).
description: Every word the app uses for something of its own, in one place.

heading: Collaboration
text:
**Collaborator**
Someone you have invited to write on a song. Each one gets their own tab and
their own colour. A song can have up to eight, you included. Older versions of
the apps said **co-writer**.

**Invite code**
A six character code, plus a share link, that lets someone join one song. It is
not an email invitation and nothing is sent for you. The recipient enters it
under Settings, Song Invite Code. See
[Inviting a collaborator](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/).

**Master tab**
The agreed version of a shared song. Anyone on the song can type in it, one
writer at a time, or send sections to it from their own tab. See
[The Master](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/master/).

**Master lock**
The lock that appears on the Master tab while someone is typing in it, in their
colour and with their initial. Only they can type until they tap the lock to let
others in, or stop typing for 30 seconds. See
[One writer at a time](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/master/#one-writer-at-a-time).

**Mailbox**
Where lines a collaborator sent you used to arrive, in version 2.21 and earlier
of the iPhone app. Sent lines now arrive as cards in the song's chat. See
[Sending lines to a collaborator](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sending/).

**Note**
A comment on highlighted words in a song. Collaborators reply, and anyone can
resolve it. See [Notes on lyrics](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/notes/).

**Alternate line**
A second option kept on the same line, after a spaced slash: `main / alt`. Only
the main line is read by most tools. See [Alternate lines](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/alternate-lines/).

**Session**
Live video and voice with collaborators inside a song, with your DAW's audio if
you share it from a computer. On the web, and on the iPhone app from version
2.23. See [Song sessions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/).

**Just a session** (web)
A session started from Home without a song. It becomes a song once someone
writes or names it. If it ends empty, it goes away and any takes move to
**Ideas**. See [Song sessions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/#just-a-session).
description: Every word the app uses for something of its own, in one place.

heading: Your account
text:
**Writer profile**
Your legal name, publisher, performing rights organisation and contact email.
These are the credits printed on a lyric sheet, and they are separate from your
display name. See [Your profile](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/profile/).

**Display name**
What collaborators see. Separate from your writer profile and from your email.

**Pro**
The paid plan. It raises the AI, rhyme and recording limits, adds in-line
suggestions and keeps your [original files](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/#original-files).
Collaboration is **not** a Pro feature, and joining a
[session](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/) is free, though starting one needs Pro. See [Plans and Pro](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/plans/).
description: Every word the app uses for something of its own, in one place.

heading: Finding a command

| Action | Mac | Windows and Linux |

| Search everything, and find any action | `⌘` `K` | `Ctrl` `K` |
| Show or hide the shortcuts for the screen you're on | `⌘` `/`, or `?` | `Ctrl` `/`, or `?` |

The keyboard button at the top of the page (in a song, **Keyboard shortcuts** in the song's ⋯ menu) does the same as
`⌘` `/`: it shows a small card in the corner listing the shortcuts for that screen. It stays
open while you work until you hide it, and shortcuts that need a selection first show dimmed.

The **command palette** searches your songs, lyrics, notes, chat, recordings,
concepts, projects and lyric sheets, and lists everything you can do on the page you're on,
with its shortcut beside it. Start typing (a lyric you remember, "rhymes",
"perform", "dark") and press `Enter`. Results from your library come first, then
commands. It's the quickest way to learn the shortcuts below, and the way to
reach an action whose keys your keyboard can't press. The magnifying glass in the
top bar opens it too. See [Search everything](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/search/).

Shortcuts that act on a panel or a list are ignored while you are typing in a
box, so they never eat a letter you meant to type.

The song page keeps one history for the lyrics, the title and the AI Context
fields, and the **Undo** and **Redo** buttons in the song bar take back
whichever changed last.

The keys work slightly differently depending on where you are typing:

- **In the lyrics**, `⌘` `Z` or `Ctrl` `Z` undoes your last change to the

- **In the title or an AI Context field**, it undoes the last change anywhere on
  the page, the same as the **Undo** button.

heading: Recording and audio
text:
Web app:
The web app uses the same plans and the same numbers, because it is the same
account. Settings, then **Usage & Stats**, shows your usage, with separate
meters for AI calls and quick AI calls. Pro can be bought in either app. See
[Plans and Pro](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/plans/).

| | Free | Pro |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Length of a single recording or import | {{limit.recording.freePerItem}} | {{limit.recording.proPerItem}} |
| Total audio stored | {{limit.recording.freeTotal}} ({{limit.recording.freeTotalHours}}) | {{limit.recording.proTotal}} (about {{limit.recording.proTotalHours}}) |

The per item cap applies to recording and to importing equally. A file you
import cannot be longer than a recording you could have made.

heading: Writing tools
text:
| | Free | Pro |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Requests | {{limit.ai.freeCalls}} total | {{limit.ai.proMonthly}} per month |

Lighter requests are metered separately and more generously:
{{limit.ai.freeCallsLowCost}} on free, {{limit.ai.proMonthlyLowCost}} per month
on Pro. These quick calls are what the automatic features use:
[in-line suggestions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/inline-suggestions/) and the rhyme sheet's
[AI picks](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/rhymes/). That is why they do not eat your main allowance.

On the free plan, the automatic features stop when the quick calls run out.
They never spend the AI calls you are keeping for the tools you choose. On Pro,
once the quick pool is used up for the month, they carry on drawing from the
main one.

[Genie chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/) has its own allowance on Pro, 1,000 messages a
month. On the free plan each message uses one of your AI calls.

Web app:
When the web app retries a request on its own, such as Wish Workshop asking
again after a reply that did not fit, or a syllable recount, the retry is not
counted.

heading: What happens at a limit
text:
Limits announce themselves. Recording past the length cap stops the take and
says so. Importing an over length file is refused with the file's length in the
message. Running out of lookups tells you when they reset.

Nothing is deleted when you hit a limit, and nothing fails silently.

text:
The **Concepts** tab holds ideas before they are songs. The
app's own description is the clearest one: concepts are creative starting points
that shape a song before you write a single word.

They live here rather than in your song list so a half-formed idea does not sit
alongside real work in progress.

iPhone and iPad app:
Each card is a title plus a mood, a theme and some similar artists. Tap one and
it expands to show the whole thing, with a button to turn it into a song.

The two buttons in the corner are the whole tab: **+** writes a concept by hand,
and the sparkle generates a batch from songs you have already written.

Web app:
Each card shows its title with the mood, theme and similar artists underneath,
labelled, so you can read a concept without opening it. Cards in a row share the
height of the tallest. Click a card to edit it in place; its boxes grow to fit
whatever you write.

Every card has a ⋯ menu in its corner: **New Song from Concept**, **Generate 3
Similar**, a row of colours to pick from, **Edit**, **Duplicate** and **Delete**.
Cards are in the order you put them, and you can drag a card to a new place in
the grid. There is a search field above the grid.

Two buttons sit in the page header: **New Concept** writes one by hand, and
**Generate** proposes a batch from songs you have already written. The empty
card at the end of the grid, **Click to Add**, does the same as New Concept.

Press **Select** (or ⌘-click or Ctrl-click a card) to pick several. Shift-click
takes a run, and ⌘A or Ctrl+A takes every card shown. The bar at the bottom
recolours, duplicates or deletes them together.
description: A grid of song ideas that are not songs yet.

heading: Where to go from here
text:
- **[Concepts](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/concepts/)** for the fields, the generator and its
  switches, and what happens when a concept becomes a song.
- **[The song wizard](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/song-wizard/)** for the other end of the same
  idea, which asks you three questions instead of proposing answers.

text:
**Home** is the first thing you see when you open Lyric Genie in a browser. It
does the job the Start tab does in the iOS app: it puts the song you were last
writing in front of you, and gives you a few quick ways into a new one.

To get back to it, click the genie logo at the top left. In a phone browser it
is the first tab in the bar along the bottom.

The top of the page greets you by name, with a different line each day. Your
name is a link: click it to [edit your profile](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/profile/).
description: Where the Lyric Genie web app opens. Pick up the song you were writing, catch an idea before it goes, and see what your collaborators did.

heading: Quick start
text:
Four round buttons sit beside the greeting on a wide window, and under it on a
narrower one. Once you scroll down they shrink to small icons in the header, so
they stay within reach.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Write** | Opens a new song and asks how you want to start: **Guide me** or **Start from scratch**. See [Guided Start](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/#guided-start). |
| **Record** | Records an idea right there on Home. A record bar opens at the bottom of the page, and the take is saved to your Ideas inbox when you save it. See [Recordings](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/). |
| **Concept** | Opens the Concepts page with a new concept ready to type. See [Concepts](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/concepts/). |
| **Session** | Opens the session lobby, where you check your camera and mic, then start a session on a song or as **Just a session**, with no song. See [Sessions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/). |

Where sessions are not available on your account, the fourth button is **Join a
song** instead, for entering a code a collaborator sent you.

Press `N` anywhere on Home to start a new song without reaching for the mouse.
It does nothing while you are typing in a box.
description: Where the Lyric Genie web app opens. Pick up the song you were writing, catch an idea before it goes, and see what your collaborators did.

heading: Searching
text:
The search box under the greeting looks through everything: songs, lyric lines
on every tab, notes, chat, recordings, ideas, concepts and projects. Results
appear as you type. See [Search everything](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/search/).
description: Where the Lyric Genie web app opens. Pick up the song you were writing, catch an idea before it goes, and see what your collaborators did.

heading: Joining a collaborator's song
text:
If none of your songs are shared yet, Home shows **Got a code from a
collaborator?** Click **Join a song** and type the code they sent you. The × hides
the card. See [Inviting a collaborator](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/#joining-a-song).
description: Where the Lyric Genie web app opens. Pick up the song you were writing, catch an idea before it goes, and see what your collaborators did.

heading: Continue writing
text:
The large card is the song you last edited yourself. An edit a collaborator made
does not count, so a shared song they were busy in overnight will not push your
own work aside.

It shows the last three lines you wrote, how many words the song has, and the
section the lyrics end in. Click **Pick up where you left off** and the song
opens with the cursor back where you left it.

The cursor position is remembered by this browser. On another computer, or
after clearing your browsing data, the song opens at the end of the lyrics
instead.

If you have no songs yet, the card says **Start your first song** instead.
description: Where the Lyric Genie web app opens. Pick up the song you were writing, catch an idea before it goes, and see what your collaborators did.

heading: Starting with Genie
text:
**Not sure where to start?** sits beside it. Click one of the three suggestions,
or type what is on your mind and press **Enter**. Lyric Genie opens a new song
with the Genie chat already open and your message sent.

That message is a real Genie message, so it counts toward your AI use. See
[Genie chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/).
description: Where the Lyric Genie web app opens. Pick up the song you were writing, catch an idea before it goes, and see what your collaborators did.

heading: Recent songs
text:
Your next six most recently edited songs, each with its first line and when it
was last changed. A shared song carries a small people icon, and a **NEW** tag
when there is something new from a collaborator since you last opened it. Point
at the tag to see what. **All songs**
opens the full list.
description: Where the Lyric Genie web app opens. Pick up the song you were writing, catch an idea before it goes, and see what your collaborators did.

heading: Since you were away
text:
What your collaborators have done on shared songs: someone accepting an invite,
changing lyrics, adding a recording, or changing a title or the AI Context. The
four most recent show here.

Click one to open that song. A lyric change opens straight on the tab of the
writer who made it, and a new recording opens the song's Recordings with that
take highlighted.

If none of your songs are shared, the card suggests inviting a collaborator from
any song. See [Inviting a collaborator](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/).
description: Where the Lyric Genie web app opens. Pick up the song you were writing, catch an idea before it goes, and see what your collaborators did.

heading: Ready to write
text:
Your three most recently changed concepts. Click one to see it on the Concepts
page, scrolled to and highlighted. **New Song** on a concept starts a song with
its title, mood, theme and similar artists already filled in, and opens it.

The last tile goes to the Concepts page, where you can generate more.
description: Where the Lyric Genie web app opens. Pick up the song you were writing, catch an idea before it goes, and see what your collaborators did.

heading: Ideas inbox
text:
Recordings that don't belong to a song yet: ones you made with **Record** on
Home or the Recordings page, or outside a song in the iOS app. Click one to play
it right there. The link at the top right opens the Recordings page with all of
them. See [Recordings](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/).
description: Where the Lyric Genie web app opens. Pick up the song you were writing, catch an idea before it goes, and see what your collaborators did.

heading: This month
text:
The row at the bottom is a quick count:

| Number | What it counts |
| --- | --- |
| **Songs touched this month** | Songs edited since the 1st. |
| **Songs** | Songs in your library, not counting archived ones. |
| **Projects** | Your projects. |
| **AI calls this month** / **Free AI calls used** | Your AI use against your plan's allowance. |

The last one reads **AI calls this month** on Pro and **Free AI calls used** on
the free plan. The numbers are on [Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: Where the Lyric Genie web app opens. Pick up the song you were writing, catch an idea before it goes, and see what your collaborators did.

text:
The **Recordings** tab is a view across all your audio. It
is not where recordings are stored, which is the distinction that trips people
up: **a recording belongs to a song**, and this tab lists them all regardless.

A row shows when it was made, how long it runs, the song it belongs to and the
writer who made it. A recording with no song yet says **Song Idea** instead, and
carries buttons for fixing that.

iPhone and iPad app:
Tap a row to expand it. You get playback, the transcript if there is one, and a
⋯ menu with export, rename, unlink, archive and delete.

Web app:
Every row shows its waveform straight away, with a play button beside the
title. Click anywhere on the waveform to play from that point; starting one
recording stops any other that is playing. Click the playing take again to
pause it (its row shows a pause icon), and again to carry on. The song name under the title is a
link to the song, and a loose recording says **Song Idea** instead. Click a
recording's name to rename it.

Under the waveform, a recording linked to lyrics shows the **Linked lyrics** it
belongs to, and otherwise its **Transcript** if it has one, in a small box with
line breaks shown as `//`. When a recording has both, a switch in the box flips
between them, and a long one opens with **Show more**. **Show in song**, beside
the linked lyrics, opens the song on the right tab, scrolls to those lines and
flashes them.

Everything else is in the row's ⋯ menu. For a recording on a song: Open Song,
Rename, Download, Archive and Delete. For a loose one: New Song from Idea, Add
to Song, Rename, Download, Archive and Delete. On Pro, a take you uploaded also
has **Download Original**, for the file exactly as you uploaded it. See
[Original files](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/#original-files). On a shared song you can
only rename, archive or delete your own takes.

Along the top are **Record** and **Upload Audio**, a search field that also
searches transcripts, an **All / In Songs / Ideas** filter, a sort menu (date,
title or song name, either direction), **Select** and **Archive**. Archive is a
toggle: while it is on, the button stays purple and a banner says you are
looking at archived recordings, with **Back to Recordings** to leave. Recording
and importing in the browser need Chrome, Edge or Safari. See
[Supported formats](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/formats/).

### Several at once

Press **Select** (or ⌘-click or Ctrl-click a recording) to pick several. Click
rows to add or remove them, Shift-click to take a whole run, and press ⌘A or
Ctrl+A for everything the list is showing. A bar at the bottom offers
**Archive** (or **Unarchive** in the archive), **Download**, **Add to Song** when
loose recordings are picked, and **Delete**. Anything an action can't touch,
such as a collaborator's take on a shared song, is left alone and counted. Press
Esc or **Done** to stop selecting.
description: Every piece of audio you have captured, in one list, whether or not it belongs to a song.

heading: Where to go from here
text:

- **[Recordings in a song](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/recordings/)** for recording while you write,
  and for tying a take to particular lines.
- **[Freestyle](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/freestyle/)** for singing first and getting lyrics back.

If you recorded something and cannot find it inside a song, it is almost
certainly sitting here unattached. See
[How it fits together](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/how-it-fits-together/).

Web app:
On a desktop, open Settings from the menu under your avatar in the top right of

heading: Usage & Stats (web)
text:
Web app:
**Usage & Stats** used to be called Stats. It has three parts, in this order.

**AI Usage** has two meters, each showing what you have used against your
plan's allowance:

- **AI calls**: Genie, Wish Workshop, Spark and the other writing tools.
- **Quick AI calls**: the lighter features, which are in-line suggestions and
  AI rhyme picks. On the free plan, when these run out those features stop, and
  your AI calls are kept for the tools you choose. On Pro they carry on with
  your AI calls.

On Pro both reset every month. On the free plan they are a total. The numbers
are on [Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).

**Voice Recording Usage** shows the recording time you have used: your own
takes, in your songs and your Ideas.

**Your Songs** counts your songs: the total, how many are solo and how many are
collaborative.

heading: Lyric Sheets (web)
text:
Web app:
**Lyric Sheets** opens a page listing every sheet you have published, with the song and the writers on it. Search them by song or writer.
Each row has **Open**, which opens the sheet in a new tab, **Copy link**, and
a bin to take the sheet down. Taking one down stops its link working for
everyone; the song itself stays.

Your sheets also turn up in [search](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/search/).

text:
The **Songs** tab is where your writing lives. It opens
on **All Songs**, newest first, and that is the list most people never leave.

Web app:
Click a row to open the song. The ⋯ at the right of a row holds everything else
you can do to it, including **Duplicate as a new song**. Along the top are a
search field, **Import Lyrics**, **Join with code**, a sort menu, **Select** and
**New Song**.

**Join with code**, or `J`, opens the box for an invite code a collaborator sent
you. See [Inviting a collaborator](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/#joining-a-song).

**Select** lets you act on several songs at once. Click rows to pick them,
Shift-click to take a run, and press ⌘A or Ctrl+A for every song in view. The
bar at the bottom offers **Add to Project**, **Remove from Project** (inside a
project), **Duplicate**, **Archive** (or **Unarchive** in Archived) and
**Delete**. Duplicate makes a copy of each as a new song of yours. See
[Duplicating a song](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/songs/#duplicating-a-song-web-app-only). Delete only
removes solo songs you own; shared songs are kept and counted, since a shared
song can only be archived. Press Esc or **Done** to stop.

A row gives you the title, when you last touched it, and the opening lines, so
you rarely have to open a song to know which one it is. A
icon beside a title means that song is shared.

Web app:
On the web the shared icon sits after the title. A row also counts the
recordings and writers on the song, and a green number at the right means
other writers are in it right now.

Under a shared song's title you see:

- **Small avatars** of everyone on the song, yours included.
- **A chat bubble with a red number** when there are chat messages you have
  not read. It clears when you read the chat. See
  [Collaborator chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/).
- **What is new since you last opened it**, such as *Sam made changes to their
  lyrics*. Opening the song clears it.

A shared song opens on the tab you were last on: your own, a collaborator's or
the Master. The web app remembers this per browser, and the iPhone app per
device (iOS 2.23).

If the song is filed in a project, a line above the title names it in that
project's colour. A song in several projects lists them, and a song in none has
no line at all. Inside a project the line only names the *other* projects a song
is in, since the screen is already titled with this one. See
[Projects](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/projects/).

iPhone and iPad app:
The buttons along the top are a bell for notifications, a ⋯ for sorting and
multi-select, and a compose button that starts a new song.

heading: Behind the back arrow
text:
The **‹** beside the title is easy to miss, and it is the only way to the rest
of the tab. It opens **Collections**, which is where All Songs itself lives
alongside everything else your songs are filed in.

Web app:
The search field matches titles, your lyrics, the mood, theme and artists, and collaborators' names. The sort menu offers
Date Created, Last Edited or Title, ascending or descending, and the web app
remembers your choice in that browser.
